On stagnation, he follows the Steindl–Kalecki line: monopoly conditions lower the propensity to invest and innovate, and redistribution towards profits depresses demand.

Sawyer concludes that market-promoting, deregulatory policy has fostered monopoly capitalism and delivered growth below that of the postwar "golden age". Analyses of monopoly capital and of financialisation together explain the near-stagnation of the past two decades. Future growth, he adds, will probably stay low for climate and environmental reasons and will have to differ structurally from past growth, an adjustment he says financialised monopoly capitalism cannot make. Read the original if you want a Post-Keynesian and Kaleckian empirical case that links neoliberalism, financialisation and Big Tech to monopoly capitalism and stagnation.
quoteEn: The neoliberal era of the past 40 years has produced growing inequality, not the higher growth rate it promised, and has hardly reduced unemployment.
quoteZh: 过去40年的新自由主义时代造成了日益严重的不平等，而不是其承诺的提高增长率，且几乎没有降低失业率。

t: Socialist thought and practice of the Venezuelan left
st: The United Socialist Party of Venezuela under Maduro
zh: 委内瑞拉左翼的社会主义思想与实践
source: Foreign Theoretical Trends (国外理论动态), 2023 no. 3
paras: This research article examines how the United Socialist Party of Venezuela (PSUV), founded by Hugo Chávez in 2008, has governed under Nicolás Maduro since 2013. Yang and Zhang argue that the party has survived the severe "Venezuelan crisis" and is now using a more favourable environment to adjust its leadership and organisation and to innovate in governing ideas and methods. They nonetheless judge that the party's governing philosophy is far from scientific socialism and is better seen as another exploration of a development path distinct from the Western model.

The article begins with the party's origins, its founding documents and Maduro's rise to the chairmanship in 2014. It then moves through five parts: the improved governing environment since about 2021; changes to leadership and organisation after the Fifth Congress (2022); the new governing concept and its practical projects; the challenges still facing the party; and a short conclusion.

On the environment, the authors cite the end of hyperinflation, GDP growth of over 15% in 2022, the party-led coalition's landslide wins in the 2020 and 2021 elections, an easing of US sanctions and the leftward turn in Latin America. On innovation, they present Maduro's "3R.Nets" concept as the core guide: resistance, rebirth and revolution, within a "new period of transition to socialism" fixed at 2022–2030. They read two initiatives through it: the "Good Government 1×10" online complaint system and the planned special economic zones meant to attract foreign investment. Organisational changes include a new 13-member Politburo, regional "contact persons" and grassroots elections in which non-party members could vote.

The authors list four challenges: the Homeland Plan 2019–2025 targets (oil output of 685,000 barrels a day in 2022 against a goal of 5 million), obstacles to the special zones such as vague incentives and weak investor trust, criticism from dissidents and the Venezuelan Communist Party that the party has drifted towards capitalism, and a legitimacy problem shown by falling turnout and votes between 2012 and 2018. They conclude that whether the party can implement these measures and meet these challenges will test its governing capacity and decide whether the economy recovers. Read the original if you want a Chinese Latin Americanist assessment of the PSUV's recent organisational and policy changes, with election and economic figures.
quoteEn: In essence, however, the PSUV's governing philosophy is far from scientific socialism; it is another exploration, in Latin America's new geopolitical environment, of a development path different from the Western model.
quoteZh: 然而，从本质上说，统社党的执政理念与科学社会主义相去甚远，是在拉美新的地缘政治环境中对不同于西方模式的发展道路的又一次探索。

glossary.explanation: The Marxist term for socialism grounded in historical materialism and the critique of political economy, as opposed to utopian socialism. Chinese scholars use it as a benchmark against which other socialist currents are measured.

t: The theoretical experiments of the French Communist Party
zh: 法国共产党的理论尝试
paras: This commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in August 2023, asks how the French Communist Party (PCF) has tried to survive and renew itself as a communist party in a developed capitalist country. Yu Hui argues that the PCF's recent theoretical and organisational experiments, built around the programme "Common France", are worth attention, but that they have not stopped its marginalisation. In Yu's reading, the party remains caught in a double bottleneck between theory and reality.

The article opens by presenting "upholding fundamental principles while breaking new ground" (守正创新) as both a worldview and a method for studying the world socialist movement. It then sets out the PCF's external and internal difficulties, links them to social contradictions in France, and describes the measures the party took in the twenty-first century. The measures discussed are the 38th Congress resolution, the Common France programme, the "Europe of the people" position and efforts to strengthen the central committee's role in grassroots organisation.

Yu identifies two kinds of challenge. Externally, the 2022 elections ended the old left–right duopoly and pointed to a three-way contest between the centre, the radical left and the far right, with Marine Le Pen's National Rally rising. Internally, Yu holds that the party's "new communism" is all-encompassing but lacks a core idea, so its policies and alliance strategies keep shifting. Yu also contends that the party has lost its ideological identity by turning from a "vanguard party" into a "mass party" and taking a "centrist road". The 32nd and 35th Congresses' radical turn and Left Front brought no lasting gains, and Jean-Luc Mélenchon's "La France Insoumise" displaced the party.

As Yu describes it, Common France sets out six goals: popular control of investment and distribution, a Sixth Republic, support for employment and development, real gender equality, an open and united France, and sustainable production. It treats the parliamentary road as preparation for overthrowing capitalism and calls for ecological, labour, information and monetary revolutions. Yu concludes that this evolution has not reversed the party's decline and that its understanding of capitalism and of socialist practice constrains its transformative aims. Read the original if you want a short Chinese academic view of the PCF's post-2020 strategy and its difficulties.
quoteEn: The French Communist Party is losing the ideological identity that marks it out as a communist party.
quoteZh: 法国共产党正在失去作为共产党的意识形态身份特征。

glossary.en: upholding fundamental principles while breaking new ground
glossary.literal: keep to what is correct, innovate
glossary.explanation: A slogan in Chinese Party discourse that combines fidelity to core principles with theoretical and practical innovation. The article uses it as a method for studying foreign communist parties.
The programme adopted by the PCF as its guiding document, intended to develop a twenty-first-century "new communism" and set out an action plan.
The label the PCF applies to its twenty-first-century theoretical orientation. The article describes it as broad but lacking a core idea.
The Leninist idea of a party made up of the most politically conscious workers who lead the masses. The article contrasts it with a "mass party".

t: The main practices of the Communist Party of Cuba in strengthening Party building
zh: 古巴共产党加强党的建设的主要做法
paras: Liang Xiaoyu asks how the Communist Party of Cuba has kept its ruling position and public credibility despite the US blockade, the shock of the Soviet and East European collapse, and a narrow economic base. The article argues that the Party has done so through a set of mutually reinforcing Party-building practices, and that these offer lessons for any Marxist ruling party.

After a short introduction to Cuba and the history of the Party, from its founding organisation in 1961 to the Eighth Congress in April 2021, the article organises the Cuban experience under four headings: ideological and theoretical work, the anti-corruption struggle, serving people's livelihood, and the mass line with close Party–people ties. A concluding section draws out four general lessons. The evidence consists of Party documents, congress decisions, membership figures and examples of cadre discipline and consultation campaigns.

Liang's core argument is that the Party's strength rests on theory that is both firmly Marxist-Leninist and localised, and on ties with ordinary people. On theory, the article describes a tiered network of Party schools and training centres and the writing of José Martí's thought into the Party statutes, which it presents as an adaptation of Marxism to Cuban conditions. On conduct and the masses, it reports strict punishment of corrupt senior officials, publicly known and modest cadre salaries, no special privileges, and mass organisations covering almost the whole population. It also describes large consultations on congress documents, citing 3.5 million participants in the debate before the Fourth Congress and over seven million in the discussion of the Sixth Congress guidelines. Free education and health care, and attention to food security, are presented as the material basis of popular support.

Liang concludes that a Marxist ruling party must accept supervision by the masses, maintain a good work style, pursue theoretical innovation rooted in national conditions, and build strong grass-roots organisations. The author holds that Cuba's experience has also advanced Marxism in the twenty-first century and carries significance for world socialism. Read the original if you want a Chinese Party-school scholar's account of how the Cuban Party's discipline, mass-line and welfare practices are presented as models for Party building.
quoteEn: Marxism can innovate and develop with the times only if it is combined with a country's national conditions and rooted in its national culture.
quoteZh: 马克思主义只有与本国国情相结合，立足于本国的民族文化，才能与时俱进地创新和发展。

glossary.explanation: A Chinese Communist Party working method, associated with Mao Zedong, of gathering views from ordinary people and returning them as policy. Here the author applies it to the Cuban Party's links with the population.
A broad Chinese term covering ideological education, organisation, discipline, work style and anti-corruption work within a ruling party.
The ideas of José Martí, the nineteenth-century Cuban independence leader. The article says the Party wrote them into its statutes alongside Marxism-Leninism.

glossary.en: the Soviet and East European collapse
glossary.literal: drastic changes in the Soviet Union and Eastern Europe
glossary.explanation: The standard Chinese term for the fall of Soviet-bloc communist governments around 1989–1991.

t: On Rosa Luxemburg's socialist conception of culture
zh: 论罗莎·卢森堡的社会主义文化观
source: Foreign Theoretical Trends (Guowai lilun dongtai), 2023 no. 3
paras: Research on historical materialism, He Ping observes, has shifted from macro-level theories of the transformation of social formations to micro-level cultural critique. The article asks how that shift occurred, how the two levels relate, and whether their theoretical gains can be joined. It takes Rosa Luxemburg's socialist conception of culture as a case study. He argues that her conception was a key turning point, produced in her fight against Millerandism, and that it links the macro theory of revolution to micro cultural critique.

The article has four parts. It first reconstructs the Millerand affair of 1899, in which a French socialist joined a bourgeois cabinet, and Luxemburg's critique of it. It then examines what the author calls the rational construction of socialist culture, drawing on her readings of Marx's early writings and of Capital. Next it covers the ideological construction of socialist culture: the concept of the working class, the critique of religion, and the party's relation to the trade unions. It ends with three lessons for current research.

He's central move is that Luxemburg recast legal reform through the dialectic of whole and part. Reform has a socialist character only if it forms a stage within the proletariat's overall struggle. Otherwise it is bourgeois, however it presents itself. On this basis she argued that Marx's doctrine is the proletariat's spiritual culture. In He's account, that culture cannot arise spontaneously within bourgeois culture. It emerges at the point of rupture with it, and the Social Democratic Party must hold cultural leadership over parliamentary and trade-union work. He reads her accounts of Marx's early development, of the rate of profit in Capital volume 3, and of religion as 'political fetishism' as parts of this project. In the same spirit she rejected Bernstein's praise of British trade unionism.

He concludes that Luxemburg's conception diagnosed the crisis of the Second International and reflected on socialist modernity. He draws three lessons. First, socialist modernity should become a topic of historical-materialist research. He argues that Western Marxism and the Eastern European Budapest School failed to distinguish capitalist from socialist modernity, and he links this to the collapse of Eastern European socialism. Second, research should look for the point where macro and micro perspectives meet. Third, a theory of socialist modernity must be built from China's own practice, not transplanted from Luxemburg. This bears on the study of Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a detailed Chinese reading of Luxemburg's writings on Millerandism, religion and trade unions, and the author's case for linking cultural critique to revolutionary theory.
quoteEn: The spirit of socialist culture is not an abstract concept but is of its time and of its nation, and therefore has very real content.
quoteZh: 社会主义文化精神不是抽象的概念，而是时代的、民族的，因而有着十分现实的内容。

glossary.explanation: The official Party formulation for China's own path of modernization, prominent in Party discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022). The article mentions it only to suggest a philosophical route for studying it.

Term for socialist participation in a bourgeois government, named after Alexandre Millerand, who joined a French cabinet in 1899. It set off a major dispute in the Second International between Marxists and revisionists.
The author's proposed research topic, set against capitalist modernity, which the author says Western Marxist critiques of modernity left unexamined.

t: An analysis of the Communist Party of Vietnam's practical model of advancing state governance
zh: 越南共产党推进国家治理的实践模式探析
paras: Xu Qinfa and Zhang Rui ask how the Communist Party of Vietnam (CPV) organises state power and why it rejects Western-style separation of powers. They argue that the CPV's "division of labour among the three powers" (sanquan fengong) is a governance model that joins Marxist-Leninist theory of state power to Vietnamese practice. In their account it differs from Western separation of powers because the powers are not separated or set against each other. State power stays unified and belongs to the people, under CPV leadership, while state organs divide tasks, cooperate and supervise one another when exercising legislative, executive and judicial power.

The article has three parts. The first traces the model's logic: its theoretical basis in Marx, Engels and Lenin, its historical development from the 1946 constitution through the 1959 and 1980 constitutions to the 2001 amendment and the 2013 constitution, and its origin in the CPV's response to "peaceful evolution". The second sets out the model's basic principles. The third discusses its practical value.

The authors identify three principles. First, the CPV exercises "overall leadership" as the sole ruling party. They say it does not directly wield state power but leads politically, organisationally and ideologically. Second, state power is unified and belongs to the people, who exercise it through direct and representative democracy as provided in the 2013 constitution. Third, the legislature (National Assembly), government and courts divide functions, cooperate and supervise one another, which the authors present as a guard against the alienation of state power. They describe calls for separation of powers, a multiparty system or "civil society" as part of peaceful evolution. They note that a 2017 Party regulation makes advocating them grounds for expulsion.

The authors conclude that the model keeps Vietnam on a socialist path, realises people's mastery of their own affairs, and helps build a clean and strong political system. They cite Vietnam's results against Covid-19 as evidence of the model's advantages. The article is largely affirmative and relies on CPV documents and speeches by Nguyen Phu Trong and Ho Chi Minh. Read the original if you want a Chinese scholarly presentation of how Vietnam's official doctrine justifies one-party rule and rejects separation of powers.
quoteEn: The CPV's \"division of labour among the three powers\" differs from the separation of powers in Western capitalist states: state powers are not separated or checked against each other. Under CPV leadership, state power is kept unified and belonging to the people, and state organs divide tasks, cooperate and supervise one another in exercising legislative, executive and judicial power.
quoteZh: 越共的“三权分工”不同于西方资本主义国家的三权分立，国家权力之间不是分立、制衡，而是在坚持越共的领导下，确保国家权力统一且属于人民，各国家机关在行使立法权、行政权、司法权时分工、配合、监督。

glossary.en: division of labour among the three powers
glossary.explanation: Vietnam's official formula, written into the 2013 constitution, for how legislative, executive and judicial power are organised. It stresses unified state power with cooperation and supervision among organs, as opposed to separation of powers.
A term used in communist-party discourse for alleged Western efforts to undermine socialist systems from within by non-military means such as ideological and political influence.
The CPV's formula for its role: it sets lines and policies and guides state organs, rather than directly exercising state power or handling specific affairs.

glossary.en: people's mastery of their own affairs
glossary.literal: the people being masters of the house
glossary.explanation: A standard socialist-state phrase for the people as the holders of state power, here applied to Vietnam.

t: Lessons and implications of the failure of the Soviet model of socialist modernization
zh: 社会主义现代化苏联模式失败的教训及启示
paras: Zhao Hong asks why the Soviet model, the first attempt to build a socialist alternative to capitalist modernization, failed, and what that failure offers to countries still exploring socialist modernization. The article argues that the Soviet experience should not be dismissed one-sidedly but weighed dialectically, since it provides, in Zhao's words, a complete 'model' running from experience to lessons for Chinese modernization.

Drawing on Barrington Moore's typology of modernization paths and on Russian and Soviet sources, including Lenin, Stalin, Gorbachev's memoirs and Deng Xiaoping, the article first diagnoses three failures. It then draws three implications for the present. The analysis runs from Peter the Great to the Soviet collapse, with extended attention to the New Economic Policy and to Stalin's economic writings.

The three failures are as follows. First, the Soviet model never escaped Russian historical and cultural tradition. Zhao describes a catch-up modernization driven by state coercion and military expansion, citing figures on military spending and territorial growth, which left living standards and political life stagnant. Second, it never resolved the relation between socialist practice and the essence of socialism. Zhao contrasts Lenin's shift from War Communism to the New Economic Policy with Stalin's pursuit of ever 'larger and purer' production relations, which Zhao says detached them from the level of the productive forces. Third, it mishandled the absorption of capitalist modern civilisation. Lenin favoured learning from foreign technology and management, whereas Stalin's late 'two parallel world markets' thesis, in Zhao's account, produced closure and a lopsided military-industrial economy.

Zhao's implications for China are that the ruling party must always put the people's interests first, citing a late-Soviet survey in which 85 per cent said the CPSU represented officials, and linking this to the Party's self-reform; that modernization must not depart from national conditions or treat Marxism as dogma; and that it must advance through mutual learning among civilisations. Zhao adds that Chinese modernization and the Soviet model are both catch-up modernizations, so resolving the imbalances this produces remains a major task. Read the original if you want a Party School scholar's account of how Soviet failure is used to frame lessons for Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: The Soviet path of modernization was a wholly new exploration begun under a socialist system, but it pursued one-sided modernization goals, which left it unable for a long time to answer the people's hopes for a better life; it ultimately departed from the essence of socialism and lost the people's trust and support.
quoteZh: 苏联的现代化道路是在社会主义制度的背景下开始的全新探索，追求的是片面的现代化目标，这使其长期无法回应人民群众对美好生活的期盼，最终背离了社会主义本质，终致失去了人民的信任和支持。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's own path of modernization under Party leadership, prominent in Party discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western modernization.
An official formula for the Party's efforts to correct its own problems, such as corruption and bureaucracy, emphasised under Xi Jinping.
The policy Lenin introduced in Soviet Russia in 1921 to replace War Communism. It restored markets and trade and relied on a worker–peasant alliance.
The emergency economic policies of 1918–1921, including requisitioning and state control, adopted during the Russian Civil War.

t: Why a great ecological civilization can emerge in socialist China
st: An interview with the ecological Marxist theorist John Bellamy Foster
zh: 为什么伟大的生态文明能够在社会主义中国产生
zhSub: 著名生态马克思主义理论家福斯特教授访谈
paras: This is an interview in which Guo Jianren of Zhongnan University of Economics and Law questions John Bellamy Foster, editor of Monthly Review and sociologist at the University of Oregon. It follows Foster's lecture "Ecological Civilization and Ecological Revolution: An Ecological Marxist Perspective", given at the invitation of the Sansheng Valley Cobb Eco-Academy. Foster's central claim is that the ecological civilization the world needs must move towards socialism, and that this is why the idea has become a real force in China but hardly exists in capitalist countries.

Guo's questions cover five topics. They ask how ecological Marxism can draw on natural science, Whitehead's organic philosophy and traditional Chinese culture, and why Foster rejects Jeremy Lent's reading of Chinese ecological civilization. They ask about the political-economic mechanisms behind ecological civilization, including monopoly capitalism and the Green New Deal. They ask about Marx's "metabolism" concepts and China's urbanisation and rural revitalisation, about the "environmental proletariat", and about China's role in global ecological governance.

Foster answers the first question through Joseph Needham, whom he presents as combining Marxism, ecological materialism, Whitehead's process philosophy and Chinese Daoist thought, all opposed to capitalism. On the second, he argues that the Western Green New Deal is only a slogan or "green Keynesianism" that the capitalist system rejects. He says monopoly capitalism produces stagnation, waste and financialisation and leaves no room for ecological civilization, whereas China treats it as a core task of socialist construction and has a roadmap for ecological transition. On the third, he says Marx's "universal metabolism of nature", "social metabolism" and "metabolic rift" form a unity. He wonders whether rapid urbanisation may widen China's rift, yet he welcomes collective rural land ownership, rural revitalisation and poverty reduction. He then proposes the "environmental proletariat", a broader class concept drawn from Engels's The Condition of the Working Class in England, which would include ecological peasants and the workers and peasants of the Global South.

Foster concludes that ecological civilization and the socialist movement reinforce each other. He describes China's ecological civilization as perhaps the greatest gift socialist development has given the world. He also notes that the idea first appeared in the Soviet Union in the 1980s. Read the original if you want Foster's own account, addressed to a Chinese audience, of ecological Marxism, his metabolic rift theory and his view of Chinese ecological civilization.
quoteEn: The core point of this lecture of mine is that the ecological civilization the world needs today must move towards socialism.
quoteZh: 我此次讲座的核心观点是，当今世界所需要的生态文明必须迈向社会主义。

glossary.explanation: A Chinese official concept, prominent since the 2000s, for a form of development that balances economic growth with environmental protection. It is now part of Party policy, and Foster reads it in a socialist and ecological Marxist sense.
Marx's idea, developed by Foster, that capitalist production breaks the natural cycle of nutrients and matter between society and nature. Foster uses it as the basis of ecological Marxism.
Foster's term for a broad working class defined by its environmental as well as economic conditions, including ecological peasants and workers in the Global South.

t: "Marxism in the Anthropocene": origins of the issue, content analysis and theoretical assessment
zh: “人类世的马克思主义”：议题源起、内容探析与理论评述
source: Journal of China University of Geosciences (Social Sciences Edition), 2023 no. 3
paras: This 2023 article, published in the Journal of China University of Geosciences (Social Sciences Edition), reviews the debate on "Marxism in the Anthropocene" that emerged in Euro-American thought around 2010. Zhao Ruifu asks what the issue actually says and how it should be assessed. The author's answer is that eco-Marxist and green-left scholars have used the Anthropocene concept to deepen the ecological critique of capitalism and to revise eco-Marxism's anthropocentric value basis and its vision of eco-socialism.

Zhao first traces the Anthropocene concept from Buffon, Stoppani, Pavlov and Vernadsky to Stoermer and Crutzen (2000) and the Anthropocene Working Group's wider impact after 2008. A chronology of texts follows: Andreas Malm's "Capitalocene" (2009), Gerda Roelvink on species-being (2013), John Bellamy Foster's formal intervention from 2015, and works by Ian Angus, Kohei Saito, Camilla Royle, Alf Hornborg and others. Zhao marks 2009, 2015 and 2019 as stages of the debate. The article ends with an assessment from the standpoint of Marxist studies, eco-Marxism and China's socialist ecological civilization.

Zhao sorts the debate into three clusters. The first concerns the start date of the Anthropocene: Foster and Saito favour the "Great Acceleration", while Malm and Hornborg reject blaming humanity as a whole and place responsibility on fossil capital. The second concerns an "update" of anthropocentrism: Foster, against what he sees as monistic anthropocentrism, defends a "dialectic of the Anthropocene" that keeps human agency within a dialectic of humanity and nature. The third concerns eco-socialist proposals, including Angus's and Foster's lists of concrete measures (16 in Foster's 2022 book) and Malm's "eco-Leninism", which Zhao says still lacks systematic form.

In assessing the issue, Zhao credits it with giving Marxism abroad new momentum and activating its ecological content. Zhao also notes a risk of Marxism being "taken up at will", citing Simon Boxley's reading as an example. The author argues that engaging with the debate would help domestic scholars overcome what Zhao sees as China's relative silence on the Anthropocene. Zhao also holds that it could supply resources for the theory and practice of socialist ecological civilization and for Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a mapped chronology and bibliography of Western eco-Marxist work on the Anthropocene, together with a Chinese scholar's view of its relevance to ecological civilization.
quoteEn: "Marxism in the Anthropocene" is not a simple evaluation or "restatement" of Marxism against the Anthropocene background, but an attempt to reach certain theoretical goals through the tension between the Anthropocene category and its theoretical products on the one hand and Marxism on the other.
quoteZh: “人类世的马克思主义”不是对马克思主义在人类世背景下做出某种单纯的评价或“复述”,而是试图通过人类世范畴及其理论产物与马克思主义之间的张力实现某种理论目标。

glossary.explanation: A Chinese official concept, promoted in Party documents since the early 2000s, for a form of development that integrates environmental protection into economic, political and cultural life. The article discusses its socialist version.

The official name for China's path of modernization, set out in Party documents especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022). One of its stated features is harmonious coexistence between humanity and nature.
A term proposed by Andreas Malm and developed by Jason W. Moore. It attributes the ecological crisis to capitalism and fossil capital, not to humanity as a whole.
Malm's proposal for a state-led, emergency-style response to ecological catastrophe, drawing on the Leninist and socialist tradition.

t: The Lao People's Revolutionary Party's exploration and practice of the people's standpoint, and its main lessons
zh: 老挝人民革命党人民立场的探索实践与主要经验
paras: Xu Qinfa and Zuo Yuntian ask how the Lao People's Revolutionary Party (LPRP) has upheld a "people's standpoint" since leading Laos through the anti-French, anti-Japanese and anti-American wars of national liberation and founding the Lao People's Democratic Republic in 1975. They argue that the Party's persistence in this standpoint explains its achievements in revolution and in the reform era, and that summarising it offers international experience for socialist countries, world socialism and the international communist movement.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the theoretical basis: the views of Marx, Engels and Lenin on the masses as makers of history and on the danger of a ruling party losing contact with them, and the thought of Kaysone Phomvihane, which the authors present as the Lao localisation of Marxism-Leninism and the Party's basic guide. The second reviews practice in three fields: perfecting the political system of people's democracy, raising living standards, and keeping open channels for gathering the people's strength. The third draws out the main lessons.

In the practice section, the authors describe the LPRP's shift from "proletarian dictatorship" to "people's democratic dictatorship" and its theory of people's democracy as a stage towards socialism, followed by the 1991 constitution and more than 140 laws by 2017. They cite figures on per capita GDP rising from US$325 in 2000 to US$2,664 in 2020, public-health coverage of 98 per cent in rural areas, and growth in schools. They also cite mass organisations, Buddhism treated as a positive force, leaders' grassroots visits, and anti-corruption rules such as asset declarations.

The authors draw three lessons. The Party builds a systematic "people's theory" from experience, arms cadres with it and spreads it among the people to win hearts. It improves Party building, in ideology, politics, organisation and conduct, so as to gather popular strength. It treats protecting the people's fundamental interests as both the starting point and the aim in meeting risks such as the Asian financial crisis, Covid-19 and Western "peaceful evolution". Read the original if you want a Chinese-academic account of the Lao Party's governance record, with dates, policy documents and statistics, as seen from the Chinese scholarship on world socialism.
quoteEn: To keep the Party's class character and nature unchanged over the long term, it must let the people's standpoint guide the improvement of its own building and hold firm to the Marxist-Leninist people's standpoint.
quoteZh: 要使党的阶级属性和性质长期不变，就必须坚持人民立场引领完善党的自身建设，坚定马克思列宁主义的人民立场。

glossary.explanation: A principle in Chinese Marxist discourse that a ruling party must base its position and policies on the interests of the people. The authors apply it to the Lao Party's theory and practice.

A term for the form of state power exercised by the people under Party leadership. The article says the LPRP adopted it in place of "proletarian dictatorship" after a plenum of its fourth Central Committee.
A term in Chinese and allied party discourse for alleged Western efforts to undermine socialist states through non-military means such as ideology and culture.

t: From the pursuit of perfect order to the practice of cultural theory
st: Zygmunt Bauman's exploration of paths beyond the crisis of modernity
zh: 从完美秩序的追寻到文化理论的实践
zhSub: 齐格蒙特·鲍曼对现代性危机超越路径的探索
source: Foreign Theoretical Trends (Guowai lilun dongtai), 2023 no. 3
paras: Among Western thinkers who have criticised modernity since the mid-twentieth century, Zygmunt Bauman is read by Zhou and Gao as offering a distinctive response to its crisis. The article argues that Bauman diagnoses the crisis through metaphors of order, then looks for a way out in culture understood as creative practice, which in their account restores human creativity and subjectivity.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the manifestations and essence of the crisis of modernity, drawing on Bauman's images of the panopticon and the gardening ambition and on his work on the Holocaust. The second treats culture as modern society's self-consciousness and as a bearer of internal ambivalence. The third turns to cultural practice as a way of dissolving the crisis, through structuration and utopian practice. The authors situate Bauman between Marx, Gramsci, Foucault, Lévi-Strauss and existentialism.

For Bauman, as the authors present him, modernity is essentially the production of order, and the drive for perfect order must expel whatever cannot be assimilated, so it produces disorder and ambivalence. The panopticon (after Foucault) and the gardener-state of Legislators and Interpreters show how this order standardises individuals; Modernity and the Holocaust treats Auschwitz as a product of the same bureaucratic and technical rationality. Culture is both creative and a tool of regulation, because humans build their social world and are bound by it. The way out lies in culture as practice rather than as structure. Structuration is endless and revolutionary activity that resists fixed order. Utopian practice, set out in Socialism: The Active Utopia, criticises alienation and historical necessity and opens possibilities without describing a concrete future society.

Zhou and Gao conclude that Bauman offers a humanist, Marxist-anthropological path beyond modernity's crisis, aimed at recovering the individual's self-determined freedom. They also note a limit. Utopia always lies ahead as a vision, supplies no specific remedy, and would be dangerous if turned into a concrete social blueprint. Read the original if you study Bauman, foreign Marxism or critical theories of modernity and want a Chinese scholarly reading that links his cultural theory to Marx and Gramsci.
quoteEn: Bauman holds that when culture as structuring practice is mastered, it can offer a workable solution for dissolving the crisis of modern society.
quoteZh: 鲍曼认为，当作为结构化的文化实践被掌握时，文化可以为现代社会危机的消解提供一种可行性方案。

t: "People-masses-first-ism" in North Korea under Kim Jong Un
zh: ​金正恩时代朝鲜的“人民群众第一主义”
paras: Li Yongchun asks how the Workers' Party of Korea under Kim Jong Un came to define its guiding ideology, "Kim Il Sung–Kim Jong Il-ism", as in essence "people-masses-first-ism" (renmin qunzhong diyi zhuyi), and what this means in practice. Li notes that scholarly work on the topic is scarce. The article argues that the formula has become the core governing idea of the Kim Jong Un era, replacing the earlier emphasis on military-first politics.

The article has three main parts followed by a conclusion. It first traces the concept through three stages: its germ in 2012, its formal proposal in 2013, and its deepening from the Seventh Party Congress (2016) to the Eighth (2021). It then sets out the concept's content, drawing on published speeches and writings by the leaders. Finally it surveys implementation in the political, economic and social fields. Li points out that the party's internal study materials on the ideology are not public, so the account rests on openly available sources.

Li presents the concept as having four components: it descends from the Kim Il Sung and Kim Jong Il maxim of treating the people as heaven; it treats the people as masters of revolution and construction; it relies on the people's strength to advance the revolution; and it requires selfless service to the people. On implementation, Li describes a sustained and public campaign against abuse of power, bureaucracy and corrupt practices, including the dismissal of officials in 2020 and a strengthened party inspection body after the Eighth Congress. Li also cites economic measures (agriculture, light industry, a livestock base, large housing projects, five-year plans) and social ones (12-year compulsory education, health facilities, cultural and tourist sites). Li reads the Eighth Congress's decision to write the concept into the party rules as the basic political method of socialism, in place of military-first politics, as a shift from "military-first" to "people-first" politics.

Li concludes that the concept has strengthened unity around Kim Jong Un and domestic stability, and says that predictions of North Korean collapse have proved wrong. Li names natural disasters, sanctions and the pandemic as the "three mountains" in the way, and expects the party to keep applying the principle to economic development and living standards. Li also expects it to be treated as a guiding ideology on a par with the Juche idea and military-first thought. Read the original if you want a Chinese scholar's account of how North Korean official sources frame Kim Jong Un's ideology and its policy applications, with dated citations of speeches and party meetings.
quoteEn: This means that "people-masses-first-ism" has formally become the core governing concept of the Kim Jong Un era, showing that the new generation of leaders has shifted the focus of national development strategy from "military-first politics" to "people-first politics".
quoteZh: 这意味着“人民群众第一主义”正式成为金正恩时代最为核心的执政理念，表明新一代领导人已经将国家发展战略的重点由“先军政治”转向“先民政治”。

glossary.explanation: The North Korean ruling party's term, first used by Kim Jong Un in 2013, for the essence of Kim Il Sung–Kim Jong Il-ism. It stresses serving the people and relying on them. The English rendering is the summary's own literal one.
The guiding ideology of the Workers' Party of Korea, established in 2012. It extends the earlier "Kim Il Sung-ism" and is built on the Juche idea.

The basic political method of the North Korean party from 2010, which gave priority to the military. The Eighth Congress in 2021 replaced it with people-masses-first politics, according to the article.
A maxim attributed to Kim Il Sung and taken up by Kim Jong Il and Kim Jong Un. The article treats it as the ideological source of the concept.
North Korea's official ideology of self-reliance and of the masses as masters of their own destiny, associated with Kim Il Sung.

t: Three misreadings of Lenin's New Economic Policy and their correction
zh: 关于列宁新经济政策的三大误读与正解
source: Contemporary World and Socialism (Dangdai shijie yu shehui zhuyi), 2023 no. 3
paras: Liu Jun and Sun Cuiping take up the question of what Lenin's New Economic Policy (NEP, introduced in 1921 in place of War Communism) actually was, and argue that it has been persistently misread. They identify three representative misreadings: the "temporary expedient" view, the "retreat" view and the "preparation for an offensive" view. Their thesis is that the NEP was a long-term, systematic exploration of how a backward country can move towards socialism by an indirect route, not a stopgap, a capitulation or a pause before attack.

The article takes each misreading in turn, citing its holders: Preobrazhensky, a 2009 Russian teachers' handbook and Ryazanovsky and Steinberg's history of Russia for the first; the Smenovekhovtsy ("change of landmarks" émigrés), Leszek Kołakowski and Evgenia Gnatenko for the second; and Zinoviev and Stalin, in the latter's late-1920s dispute with Bukharin, for the third. It then sets out three methodological principles for reading the NEP correctly. These are drawn from Lenin's own texts and linked to remarks by Deng Xiaoping, Xi Jinping and the 20th Party Congress report (2022).

Against the first view, the authors stress Lenin's phrase that the policy would be pursued "seriously and for a long time" and was meant to carry Russia through the whole transition period. Against the second, they argue that state capitalism under the dictatorship of the proletariat is capitalism that the workers' state can restrict and delimit, so the NEP changed the method of economic construction, not the nature of the state. Against the third, they read Lenin's call to "halt the retreat" as meaning no further concessions, not an end to the NEP, and as calling for regrouping and selecting capable personnel rather than attacking. They treat his talk of an "offensive" as a way of placating radicals in the Party.

The three principles are the dialectical unity of the universal and the particular in historical development, of retreat and advance, and of using capitalism and going beyond it. The authors note that state control of land and of the commanding heights of production formed the bottom line that guaranteed the NEP's socialist character. They conclude that the NEP was the first exploration of developing productive forces beyond a single form of public ownership, and that it offers lessons for reform in China. These include keeping public ownership dominant while using markets and multiple forms of ownership in the primary stage of socialism. Read the original if you want a Chinese scholarly reading of the NEP that draws on Lenin's texts and ties them to current Chinese debates on reform and the relation to capitalism.
quoteEn: The New Economic Policy was not a "temporary" expedient but a long-term institutional exploration and systematic construction of socialist development.
quoteZh: 新经济政策并非一种“暂时”的权宜之计，而是一项长期的社会主义建设的制度探索和系统建构。

glossary.explanation: The policy adopted in Soviet Russia in 1921 that replaced War Communism with a grain tax, limited private trade and state capitalism. Chinese scholarship often treats it as a precedent for reform in a socialist country.
The Bolshevik economic policy of 1918–1921, under civil war conditions, based on grain requisition and centralised control of production and distribution.

In Lenin's usage under the NEP, capitalist enterprise (concessions, leases, cooperatives) operating under the control of the proletarian state. The article stresses that it differs from state capitalism in a capitalist country.
The official Chinese characterisation of the country's present historical stage, which justifies a mixed ownership structure and the use of markets.

t: The shifting centre of gravity of the world socialist movement and China as its mainstay
zh: 世界社会主义运动重心转移现象与中国成为社会主义事业中流砥柱
source: Studies on Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping Theories, 2023 no. 1
paras: Wang Chuanli and Zhu Siyuan ask why leadership of the world socialist movement has moved from country to country, and where it now lies. Their thesis is that uneven development explains the shifts, and that China, under the leadership of the Communist Party, has become the mainstay (zhongliu dizhu) of the movement's revival. They present this as the realisation of Lenin's thesis of a "backward Europe and advanced Asia".

The article has three parts. The first traces the movement's centre of gravity through Britain (Chartism), France (June 1848 and the Paris Commune), Germany (the Second International) and Russia (the October Revolution and the Third International), relying mainly on quotations from Marx, Engels and Lenin. The second sets out four reasons why China now holds this role. The third discusses the world significance of socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era.

The authors argue that shifts depend on objective circumstances and subjective preparation. Objective conditions are decisive, but once they mature a strong proletarian party becomes the key factor, as in the case of the Bolsheviks. They contend that the Communist Party of China meets this condition. Their reasons are its handling of the collapse of the Soviet Union and Eastern Europe, its adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context, its "Chinese solution" to global disorder, and its size, discipline and capacity for self-reform. They compare it with the Soviet, Eastern European, Western European, Greek and Japanese communist parties, all of which they say failed in some respect. In the third part they claim that China's success refutes Fukuyama's "end of history", Western-centrism and Huntington's "clash of civilizations". They say it offers developing countries a path to Chinese modernization that avoids colonial plunder and dependence.

The authors conclude that the new era marks the start of the epoch Mao Zedong predicted in 1962. In their account, China's "new form of human civilisation" shows the superiority of socialism over capitalism and points the way to the revival of world socialism, to modernization in developing countries and to peaceful development. The article is a Party-aligned, openly affirmative account of China's global role. Read the original if you want to see how Chinese Marxist scholars periodise the history of the world socialist movement and justify China's claim to lead it.
quoteEn: The development of the world socialist movement is uneven, and which nation can temporarily hold the leading position depends mainly on two aspects: objective circumstances and subjective preparation.
quoteZh: 世界社会主义运动的发展是不平衡的，究竟哪一个民族能暂时占据领导地位，主要取决于客观形势和主观准备两个方面。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official term for China's own path to modernization, stressed since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is described as people-centred, aiming at common prosperity and peaceful development, and as distinct from the Western model.
The official name for the Party's theory, path and system since the reform era. It combines Marxist principles with China's conditions.
A Party formulation for the civilisational outcome of Chinese modernization. It is presented as going beyond both Western capitalist civilisation and earlier socialist models.

t: The impact of the new round of left-wing governments on Latin America's socialist movement
zh: 新一轮左翼执政对拉美社会主义运动的影响
source: Contemporary World and Socialism (Dangdai shijie yu shehuizhuyi), 2023 no. 3
paras: Writing in 2023, Yuan Dongzhen asks how the recent return of left-wing governments in Latin America has affected the region's socialist movement, and what this shows about the link between the left and socialism. The article argues that the new round of left rule has improved the overall environment for socialism, while the movement's development remains constrained by party weaknesses, left–right alternation and outside hostility.

The article first sets out three features of the new left cycle: its clustered, region-wide character, its cyclical nature, and its spillover effects. Yuan traces the first 'pink tide' from Venezuela in 1998–99, the right-wing turn after 2015, and the left's return from Mexico (2018) to Brazil (2022–23). The second part examines four effects on socialism, drawing on cases from Venezuela, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Uruguay and Bolivia. A short conclusion draws the lessons together.

Yuan argues that left governments are more favourable to socialism than right-wing ones. In the author's account, the left's social base, support for state intervention and social equity, and anti-US foreign policy overlap with socialist positions. The author holds that rising phases of Latin American socialism have coincided with left cycles and low points with right cycles. The author cites the right-wing Lima Group and Prosur, which targeted Venezuela and have since dissolved, and the restored diplomatic ties with Caracas after 2020, as evidence that pressure on '21st-century socialism' has eased. Yuan also reports that communist parties in Brazil, Chile and Colombia have become governing partners, and that left parties, regional bodies and intellectuals keep up a critique of capitalism and neoliberalism.

In conclusion, Yuan identifies limits. Many left parties, such as Ecuador's Citizen Revolution and Bolivia's Movement for Socialism, are said to be organisationally immature, dependent on charismatic leaders and prone to clientelism and bureaucratism. Frequent left–right alternation means socialism can advance only gradually and in waves. Yuan adds that US and European conservative forces continue to oppose it, and that this resistance will be hard to remove in the short term. Read the original if you want a Chinese academic's survey of the 2018–2023 left cycle in Latin America, including detailed data on communist party participation in government.}
quoteEn: The development of left-wing forces in Latin America is closely tied to the development of the region's socialist movement.
quoteZh: 拉美左翼力量的发展与该地区社会主义运动的发展有紧密的关联。

glossary.explanation: A label for the socialist projects promoted by left governments in Venezuela, Bolivia and Ecuador, associated especially with Hugo Chávez from the mid-2000s.
A term for the wave of left and centre-left election victories in Latin America from the late 1990s, 'pink' signalling a milder shade than red.

t: From left-wing guerrilla to left-wing ruling party: the experience of Nicaragua's Sandinista National Liberation Front
zh: 从左翼游击队到左翼执政党：尼加拉瓜桑地诺民族解放阵线的经验
paras: Li Han asks how Nicaragua's Sandinista National Liberation Front (FSLN) turned itself from a guerrilla organisation into a lasting left-wing party of government. The article presents the FSLN as a rare success among Latin American guerrilla movements: of the 127 armed groups active between 1980 and 2010, only 15 tried to form parties, and the author cites a success rate of about 4% for new parties in the region. Li's thesis is that the FSLN's transition and its continuous rule since 2006 rest on organisational strength, discipline, broad social alliances and growing pragmatism, though new governing problems now threaten that position.

The article has three parts. The first traces the transition from guerrilla force to party, from the 1961 founding under Carlos Fonseca through the 1979 revolution, the electoral defeat of 1990 and the return to office in 2006–2007. The second explains the party's long hold on power. The third lists the difficulties the FSLN faces after Daniel Ortega's re-election in 2021, and a short assessment places the party within the Latin American left.

On the transition, Li points to the party's inherited vertical command structure, a national leadership, provincial and municipal committees and base committees, and to the discipline reinforced after the split of 1995 and the 2002 statute. Li also stresses its alliances with trade union, peasant, women's and youth organisations, and its shift from open Marxism-Leninism in the 1980s towards a pragmatic 'Christian, socialist, solidarity' Nicaragua. On continuity in power, Li cites reconciliation with the Church and private business, economic growth and poverty reduction (national poverty down from 42.5% to 24.9% between 2009 and 2016), low homicide rates, and a stand against US hegemony. Li adds that the party controls the army and police, which it created, a feature said to distinguish it from many other left-wing governing parties. Li also cites the fragmentation of the opposition and ties with left-wing governments in the region and with China.

Li identifies four challenges: rigid organisation, an incomplete theoretical system and weak cadre development; economic contraction in 2018–2020 and falling foreign aid; the unresolved political and social crisis that began in 2018; and Western sanctions and non-recognition of the 2021 election. Li concludes that the FSLN is a pragmatic Latin American left party with some social-democratic traits, with deep social roots but defects it struggles to overcome. Read the original if you study Latin American left-wing parties, the transformation of guerrilla movements into parties, or Chinese scholarly assessments of the Sandinista government.
quoteEn: The FSLN's successful transformation from a guerrilla force into a left-wing party, and its continued development, are mainly attributed to its emphasis on organisational building, its steadily strengthened party cohesion, its attention to widening the party's social base, and its increasingly pragmatic ideas.
quoteZh: 桑解阵从游击队成功转型为左翼政党并持续发展，主要归因于它注重组织建设、不断增强政党凝聚力、重视扩大党的社会基础、思想理念更加务实。

glossary.explanation: The nationalist, anti-imperialist ideas associated with Augusto César Sandino, which the FSLN combined with Marxism-Leninism.

t: The First International and the historical origins of socialist parties' external exchanges
zh: 第一国际与社会主义政党对外交往的历史起源
source: Scientific Socialism (科学社会主义), 2023 no. 3
paras: Scholars disagree about when party diplomacy began: some trace it to the First and Second Internationals, others to the October Revolution or the Third International, and others reject any origin before 1919. Yang and Wang take up this dispute as a weakness in the basic theory of party diplomacy. They argue that the International Working Men's Association (1864) marks the historical origin of socialist parties' external exchanges, which they distinguish from party diplomacy proper.

The article first builds a conceptual framework. It separates 'external exchanges' by parties not yet in power from 'party diplomacy' by ruling parties, and it sets out the content, values and origins of socialist external exchanges. It then examines the First International's practice: support for strikes, national liberation and the Paris Commune; its statutes; its programmatic tactics; and its opposition to imperialist war. Finally it draws out the International's theoretical views and legacy.

The authors rest the argument on a few moves. They hold that external exchanges belong to parties not in power, and so form the logical precursor of party diplomacy. They read the International's statutes as guaranteeing each member's ideological, organisational and action independence, and they derive from this a rule: independence and joint action condition each other. They also argue that the International's rise and eventual collapse show that struggle requires strong party leadership. They describe its tactics as 'firm in substance, moderate in form' and as 'unity and sincere criticism', combined with open struggle against sectarian currents such as Proudhonism and Bakuninism.

Yang and Wang conclude that the International's practice was early and tentative but laid the foundations for later socialist external exchanges and for the party diplomacy of socialist states. They call for stronger theoretical awareness of the principles and tactics involved, for leadership of external exchanges by the party, and for the Marxist theory of inter-party relations to be combined with national conditions. They also say this work can supply resources for the Communist Party of China's own theory of party diplomacy. Read the original if you study the history of inter-party relations, the First International, or how Chinese scholars ground party diplomacy theory in Marxist classics.
quoteEn: Socialist parties' external exchanges must be led by the party, and party leadership is the fundamental guarantee of such exchanges.
quoteZh: 社会主义政党对外交往必须由政党领导,政党领导是社会主义政党对外交往的根本保证。

glossary.explanation: The international activity of a ruling party, which uses inter-party consultation to promote relations between states. Chinese scholars treat it as a distinct field of study and practice.
In this article, the foreign-facing activities of a party that does not yet hold state power. The authors set it against party diplomacy, which belongs to ruling parties.
The International Working Men's Association, founded in London in 1864 with Marx's involvement. It was dissolved in the 1870s.
Relations among political parties across borders. The article treats Marx and Engels's views on this as the theoretical basis of socialist parties' external exchanges.

t: The social regulation of digital capitalism
st: How platforms govern
zh: 数字资本主义的社会调节
orig: Big Data & Society, vol. 10, no. 1, 2023
source: Foreign Theoretical Trends (Guowai lilun dongtai), 2023 no. 2
paras: This is a Chinese translation of an article by Petter Törnberg, published in Big Data & Society. It asks whether digital platforms mark a break with neoliberal capitalism or an intensification of it. Using regulation theory, Törnberg argues that digital capitalism is both a continuation of financialised post-Fordism and a rupture with it. Its common core, in his account, is the digitalisation, privatisation and financialisation of market regulation.

The article first places digital capitalism within the history of capitalist transformation, tracing the shift from Fordism (state-regulated national markets) to post-Fordism (state-regulated transnational markets) to platform-owned proprietary digital markets. It then examines how platforms compete with states, drawing on cases such as Uber, Amazon, Alphabet and Meta. Finally, it analyses three shifts in social regulation: from neoliberalism to techno-feudalism, from Taylorist hierarchy to algorithmic groups, and from postmodern to automated consumer culture.

Törnberg contends that platform profit rests on rents extracted by controlling access to key resources, through infrastructural lock-in, data monopolies and network effects. Platforms exploit regulatory grey areas, expand quickly with venture capital, and present themselves as neutral to shift legal responsibility, as when Uber labels drivers "independent contractors". Platforms thus take over functions once performed by public institutions, such as setting market rules, enforcing contracts and organising labour relations. In his view this produces a "predatory" form of governance, closer to feudal lordship than to classic neoliberal markets. It also brings algorithmic control of workers and consumption shaped by manipulation, resting on what he calls a "techno-liberal" faith in the algorithmic invisible hand.

Törnberg concludes that digitalisation, since digital goods can be reproduced at near-zero cost, leads platforms to create artificial scarcity. He cites scholars who therefore see a pre-capitalist rather than post-capitalist outcome. Drawing on Gramsci, he describes the present as an interregnum and outlines three paths: continued laissez-faire platform capitalism; state use of platform capacities for control; or treating platform infrastructure as a public utility, possibly through platform cooperativism. He insists the outcome remains open and political, and that code must be subordinated to political life. Read the original if you want a regulation-theory account of platform power and its links to financialisation, rent and the state.
quoteEn: Code is institution, code is regulation, code is politics, and therefore code must be subordinated to political life.
quoteZh: 代码是制度，代码是调节，代码是政治，因此代码必须服从于政治生活。

glossary.explanation: A school of political economy, originating in France in the 1970s, that explains capitalism's historical stability through regimes of accumulation and the institutions and norms that regulate them.
The mass-production, mass-consumption regime of accumulation dominant from the Second World War to the mid-1970s, associated with Keynesian welfare states.
The regime following the crisis of Fordism, marked by flexible production, globalisation, financialisation and neoliberal policy.
A term used by Cédric Durand and others for platform capitalism, in which profit comes from rents and non-productive appropriation rather than production.

t: An analysis of Lenin's strategy for socialist moral education
zh: 列宁社会主义道德教育方略论析
source: Research on Socialist Core Values, 2023 no. 2
paras: He Jinglei asks how Lenin approached moral education under socialism and what it offers China today. The article opens from the 20th Party Congress (2022) report, which makes civic moral construction a strategic task of the Party, and from the need to cultivate a new generation fit for national rejuvenation. He argues that Lenin, though he never used the term 'socialist morality' directly, developed a systematic strategy of socialist moral education for an economically and culturally backward country.

The article is organised in five parts, each presented as one principle of Lenin's approach: making the masses the main actors; setting clear goals; building the educational environment by breaking with the old and establishing the new; applying systems thinking to the overall layout of practice; and strengthening the political leadership and exemplary role of the Communist Party. He draws mainly on Lenin's writings from the pre-revolutionary years, the period after October 1917, and the New Economic Policy.

In He's account, Lenin set five goals: a sense of ownership among working people, collectivism, a sense of role models, correct internationalism and patriotism, and loyalty to the communist cause. To create a favourable environment, Lenin called for criticising bourgeois morality and petty-bourgeois habits, intensifying Marxist propaganda and a Party press, and using trade unions, the Communist Youth League and schools as moral educators. The author identifies four practical pillars: youth as the strategic starting point, communist ideals and convictions (with realism about how long and winding the road is), discipline of several kinds, and communist labour such as the 'communist subbotniks'.

He concludes that, although Lenin's thinking bears a Russian and period imprint, it sets out general requirements, ways of thinking and points of action for moral education in less developed countries. The article presents it as relevant to cultivating a new generation for the new era, to civic moral construction, and to the goal of making China a strong socialist modernised education power. Read the original if you want a Chinese-language synthesis of Lenin's scattered remarks on morality, discipline and the Party's role, framed for current Chinese moral-education policy.
quoteEn: The Communist Party is a vanguard composed of the most class-conscious, most advanced and most active part of the working class.
quoteZh: 共产党是工人阶级中最有觉悟、最先进、最积极的部分所组成的先锋队

glossary.en: a new generation for the new era
glossary.explanation: A phrase in recent Party discourse for young people expected to combine moral, intellectual, physical, aesthetic and labour development and carry out national rejuvenation.
A Party-led programme to raise public moral standards and civility, which the 20th Party Congress report listed as a strategic task.

glossary.zh: 共产主义星期六义务劳动
glossary.explanation: Unpaid voluntary work first organised by Russian railway workers in 1919, which Lenin hailed as a 'great beginning' of communist labour.

t: Lenin's critique of Russian Narodism and its contemporary implications
zh: 列宁对俄国民粹主义的批判及其现实启示
source: Scientific Socialism (科学社会主义), 2022 no. 5
paras: Xu Wenwen asks why and how Lenin set out to criticise Russian Narodism (populism) at the turn of the twentieth century, and what that critique offers today. The article argues that Lenin's critique was not a routine intellectual quarrel. It aimed to build a "scientific ideology" and establish Marxism as the only scientific revolutionary theory, combining construction with refutation. Xu presents this as consistent with the present-day call to unite the constructive and the critical in ideological work.

The article has four parts. The first sets out why the intellectual dispute needed Lenin's judgement: Russia's cultural choices during its social transition, the long evolution of Narodism from Herzen through revolutionary and liberal phases to the Socialist Revolutionaries, and the shortcomings of earlier critics. These critics were the "legal Marxists" and Plekhanov. The second part reconstructs Lenin's critique. The third draws out its essence. The fourth turns to implications for China.

In Xu's account, Lenin made three main criticisms. He rejected the Narodniks' "non-capitalist" path by using statistics on peasant differentiation and the growth of the domestic market to show that capitalism was developing in Russia. He traced the petty-bourgeois roots of Narodism, which in his view was the ideology of the peasant democracy and a utopia that was also an expression of a historically limited democratic struggle. He also attacked Mikhailovsky's "subjective sociology" for starting from human nature rather than objective economic facts. Xu adds that Lenin defended historical necessity as compatible with individual action and the role of leaders. Lenin also held that no non-class ideology exists, so the proletariat must lead ideologically.

Xu concludes that Lenin's critique is a matter of political principle. Quoting Xi Jinping's remark that positive publicity does not mean giving up the struggle in public opinion, the author draws four lessons for China in the new era. These are to confront erroneous trends and draw a line between Marxism and anti-Marxism; to strengthen theoretical confidence in socialism with Chinese characteristics; to proceed from national conditions and develop Marxism through contemporary practice; and to uphold Party leadership and discourse power in ideological work. Read the original if you want a Chinese Party-theory reading of Lenin's early polemics and of how they are applied to current ideological work.
quoteEn: Lenin's critique of Russian Narodism was a question of whether Russia would uphold and develop Marxism.
quoteZh: 列宁对俄国民粹主义的批判，是关于俄国是否坚持和发展马克思主义的问题。

glossary.explanation: The Russian Narodnik movement of the nineteenth century, which looked to the peasant village commune as the basis of a distinctive path to socialism that bypassed capitalism.
Russian intellectuals of the 1890s, such as Struve, who used Marxist economic analysis in the legally published press. They did so to justify capitalist development, not revolution.
A term the article attributes to Lenin for Marxism as a class-based but scientific worldview. It is meant to guide the workers' movement against bourgeois and petty-bourgeois ideas.
The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's path of socialist development since reform and opening up.

t: Lenin's communist faith and flexible measures of socialist construction in spring 1918
zh: 1918年春列宁的共产主义信仰和灵活的社会主义建设措施
paras: Yu Min opens with Xi Jinping's January 2022 remark that strategy and tactics stand in a dialectical relationship, so that firmness of strategy must be combined with flexibility of tactics. The article asks how Lenin combined the two in spring 1918, between the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk in March and the outbreak of civil war in July. Yu's thesis is that in this period Lenin held unwavering faith in communism while advocating flexible measures to develop Soviet Russia's industry and economy.

The article has three parts. The first sets out four strands of Lenin's communist conviction. The second reads Lenin's call to "go our own way" and sets out six flexible measures. The third assesses Lenin's thought, tracing the same pairing to Marx and Engels and then to Deng Xiaoping and Xi Jinping. The main sources are Lenin's The Immediate Tasks of the Soviet Government, his "Left-Wing" Childishness and the Petty-Bourgeois Mentality, and his speeches of 1918.

For conviction, Yu argues that Lenin saw Soviet achievements as part of a world socialist movement. Lenin treated the economic task as one link in a chain leading to international revolution. He expected a "new giant" of revolution to grow in the West, and he called the struggle for grain "living socialism". For flexibility, Yu lists strict labour discipline, well-paid bourgeois specialists, compromise with the old co-operatives, a reworked Taylor system, German-style state capitalism, and learning management from trust organisers. Yu stresses that these departed from principle, for example the Paris Commune rule on pay, and from Marx and Engels's original vision. In Yu's reading Lenin took these steps because he started from actual conditions rather than from dogma. Lenin also rejected 'Left' Bolshevik objections that quoted Marx.

Yu concludes that Lenin continued and enriched the Marxist tradition of joining firm principle to flexible tactics, which Marx and Engels had shown in the Communist Manifesto. The author then argues that the Chinese Communists have kept this tradition through reform and opening up and in the new era. As evidence Yu cites Deng Xiaoping's remarks on communist ideals and Xi Jinping's statements, together with the poverty-alleviation campaign. Yu says that the new era's Party has enriched Lenin's thought on a higher footing. Read the original if you want a Chinese scholarly reading of Lenin's 1918 economic policy that links it to current Party theory on strategy and tactics.
quoteEn: Lenin, by contrast, proceeded from the practice of production and construction in Soviet Russia, exploring the path of construction while setting out the spirit of uniting firmness of principle and belief with flexibility of fighting tactics.
quoteZh: 列宁则是立足于苏俄生产建设的实践，一边进行生产建设并探索建设的路径，一边阐述把原则和信仰的坚定性与斗争策略的灵活性统一起来的精神。

glossary.explanation: In Lenin's 1918 usage, a form of capitalist enterprise tied to and supervised by the Soviet state, which he saw as a step forward and an intermediate link towards socialism in a small-peasant country.

A phrase from Lenin's 1918 text, which the author reads as keeping to the chosen revolutionary course while setting policy from actual conditions. The author notes it is distinct from the Chinese Communist Party's later use of the phrase.
A system of scientific management devised by the American engineer Frederick Taylor, which standardised workers' movements and output. Lenin judged it harsh but scientifically advanced.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in China from 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.

keywords: Immediate Tasks of the Soviet Government

t: New trends in Sri Lanka's socialist movement
zh: 斯里兰卡社会主义运动的新动向
paras: Du Min asks what role Sri Lanka's left-wing parties played in the economic and political crisis that, in the author's account, brought down the Gotabaya Rajapaksa government and led to the declaration of national bankruptcy in July 2022. The article also asks how the crisis changed the socialist movement. Du argues that the crisis pushed the left towards three shifts: new strategy, a broader ideological appeal and a wider political base.

The article first sorts Sri Lankan left parties into traditional (the Lanka Sama Samaja Party and the Communist Party), new (the People's Liberation Front, JVP) and radical (the National Freedom Front and the Frontline Socialist Party), and sets out how they read the crisis. It then covers strategy, ideological struggle and political foundations, and ends with the reasons for these changes. Du draws on party statements, rallies and campaigns from 2020 to 2022.

On strategy, Du describes a weakening of the 'politics of dependence', in which traditional left parties tied themselves to the Sri Freedom Party and the Rajapaksa family. A conversion of 'politics of confrontation' from armed struggle to non-violent street and parliamentary opposition has also occurred, and a 'politics of policy' is strengthening. The last includes crisis-exit programmes and the traditional left's 'solidarity economy', which would transfer loss-making firms to employee ownership. On ideology, the parties tie the crisis to capitalism and neoliberalism, claim patriotism for socialism against racialized nationalism, and stress ethnic equality and class analysis. On organisation, Du points to the National People's Power alliance, the 2022 'Supreme Alliance' of radical and traditional parties, and a push to mobilise peasants.

Du attributes these trends to three needs: rescuing the nation, winning the ideological contest against non-Marxist explanations of the crisis, and acting independently of bourgeois parties. The article presents the movement as being in a stage of a 'new revolution' after crisis, in Engels's phrase, and argues that workable policy proposals are a precondition for popular recognition. Read the original if you want a detailed, Chinese-language account of how Sri Lanka's left parties differ and how a Chinese Marxist scholar interprets their strategy after 2020.
quoteEn: Putting forward effective policy proposals is a precondition for winning popular recognition, and also a way of showing the people one's capacity to govern in future.
quoteZh: 提出有效的政策方案，是获得民众认同的前提，也是向人民彰显未来执政能力的一种方式。

t: Subject and revolution: the transformation and development of themes in Western Marxist theory
zh: 主体与革命：西方马克思主义理论主题的嬗变及发展
paras: Miao Cuicui asks how Western Marxism has handled the problem of revolution after the proletarian revolution Marx anticipated failed to occur in the developed capitalist West. The article, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in June 2023, contends that Marxist theory takes different themes in East and West: in socialist countries it stresses objective laws and scientific character, while in the West it stresses subjective agency, critique and humanism. On the theme of subject and revolution, Miao traces a line from awakening a missing class consciousness, through critique of the ideological state apparatus, to the remaking of new revolutionary subjects.

The article begins with the historical emergence of proletarian revolution in early capitalism and the predicament it later met: capitalism flourished, the Soviet Union dissolved, and Western liberal democracy proclaimed the 'end of ideology' and 'end of history'. Miao then reviews, in order, Lukács, Gramsci, the Frankfurt School (Horkheimer, Adorno, Marcuse) and Habermas. The final section turns to contemporary radical left thinkers: Negri, Hardt, Virno, Kojin Karatani, Giorgio Agamben and Alain Badiou, with Žižek cited as a framing voice.

Miao argues that the early Western Marxists located the failure of revolution in missing consciousness rather than immature material conditions. Lukács's theory of reification distinguished psychological from imputed class consciousness, while Gramsci pursued cultural hegemony through a 'war of position'. Frankfurt School critiques of the culture industry and technology, and Habermas's discourse ethics, could not, in Miao's view, shake the ideological state apparatus because cultural critique lacks a real force behind it. The theme therefore shifted to new subjects along four routes: the 'multitude' in production (Negri, Hardt, Virno), consumer boycott in consumption (Karatani), resistance to the state of exception in everyday life (Agamben), and fidelity to the 'event' in politics (Badiou).

Miao concludes that these contemporary constructions of political subjects set difference against capitalist uniformity but centre on independent, decentred individuals, and so cannot achieve real enlightenment, freedom or individuality. In the author's view, only by fusing the individual into the social human whole, and individual freedom into the proletariat's self-emancipation and human emancipation, can power be reversed and a true force for changing the world be found. Read the original if you want a compact Chinese-language overview of how a Chinese Marxist scholar sketches the Western Marxist development from class consciousness to the multitude and the event, together with the author's critique of it.
quoteEn: Only by fusing the individual into the social human whole, and fusing individual freedom into the historical process of the proletariat's own emancipation and human emancipation, on the basis of the unity of individuality and humanity, can power be reversed, the subject be reborn, and the true force for changing the world be found.
quoteZh: 只有将个体熔铸于社会性的人类整体之中，把个人的自由熔铸在无产阶级自身解放和人类解放的历史进程之中，在个性与人类性相统一的基础上，才有可能实现权力的翻转和主体的新生，才有可能找到变革世界的真正力量。

t: Lenin's communist conviction and flexible measures of socialist construction in spring 1918
zh: 1918年春列宁的共产主义信仰和灵活的社会主义建设措施
source: Marxist Studies (マルクス主义研究 / Makesizhuyi yanjiu), 2023 no. 3
paras: Yu Min opens with Xi Jinping's January 2022 remark that strategy and tactics stand in a dialectical relationship, so that firmness of strategy must be combined with flexibility of tactics. The article takes this as a method for reading Lenin's thought in spring 1918, the period between the Brest-Litovsk peace (March) and the outbreak of civil war (July). Yu argues that Lenin at once held an unshakeable communist conviction and advocated flexible measures to develop Soviet industry, and that the two embody this unity.

The article has three parts. The first sets out four strands of Lenin's conviction. The second takes his phrase "walking one's own road" from The Immediate Tasks of the Soviet Government and examines six flexible measures. The third assesses Lenin's thought against Marx and Engels, Deng Xiaoping and Xi Jinping.

On conviction, Yu reads Lenin's statements as showing that he treated Soviet achievements as part of the world socialist movement and as a torch for revolution elsewhere. He saw the economic effort as a "link" leading to the next one, international proletarian revolution. He expected a "new giant" of Western revolution to grow, and he cast the struggle for grain as a fight for "living socialism". On flexibility, Yu lists six measures. These were strict labour discipline, a high-salary system for bourgeois specialists, compromise with old cooperatives, a reformed Taylor system, German-style state capitalism, and learning management from trust organisers. Yu stresses that Lenin chose each from concrete conditions, not from theory or principle, and that he accepted tension with Paris Commune principles.

Yu concludes that Lenin continued the Marx–Engels tradition, visible in the Communist Manifesto, of joining the final goal to present struggle, and developed it through practice instead of theory alone. Yu says the Chinese Communists' practice shows the same continuity, citing Deng Xiaoping's remarks on communist ideals and Xi Jinping's on ideals as the "calcium" of the spirit and on people-centred development. In Yu's view, the Party in the new era follows Lenin's spirit and enriches it from a higher standpoint. Read the original if you want a Chinese scholarly reading of Lenin's 1918 economic policy, framed through Xi Jinping's strategy-and-tactics formula.
