As long as left forces advocating an alternative to capitalism remain marginal and the socialist movement does not revive, Li argues, populist mobilization alone cannot relieve the hardship of lower- and middle-income Italians. Read the original if you want a statistics-heavy, Marxist-inflected account of Italian welfare capitalism and its politics, written from within the Chinese debate on foreign Marxism.
quoteEn: Italy's worsening "new material scarcity" crisis stems not only from an unjust system of wealth distribution but is also closely tied to the "democratic deficit" of representative democracy.
quoteZh: 意大利呈恶化态势的“新物质匮乏”危机，不仅源于不公正的财富分配制度，还与代议制民主的“民主赤字”密切相关。

t: A historic debate over the concept of "revolution" and its present-day lessons
st: An examination of the German "November Revolution"
zh: “革命”概念的一次历史大争论及其现实启示
zhSub: 对德国“十一月革命”的考察
paras: Lai Qingli asks how the different currents of German socialism understood "revolution" during the November Revolution of 1918–1919, and what that history teaches today. Earlier scholarship, Lai says, mostly lamented the defeat and denounced the Social Democratic right for betraying the revolution, and rarely studied the conceptual dispute. The article argues that each current grasped only part of the concept, and that this one-sided, structurally unbalanced understanding helped doom the revolution.

The article first outlines the revolution's three phases, from the October 1918 sailors' mutiny to the fall of the Bavarian Soviet Republic in May 1919. It then compares right (Ebert, Scheidemann, Bernstein), centre (Kautsky) and left (Luxemburg, Liebknecht, and council advocates such as Richard Müller) on three questions. These are the means of revolution, its goals, and its essence, meaning why revolt at all and what kind of "civilisation" it should build. A concluding part draws lessons for socialist development.

On means, Lai says the right used democracy passively and treated the republic as the revolution's endpoint. The centre promised to remake democracy but stayed rhetorical, and the left sought to break bourgeois democracy through violence and workers' and soldiers' councils. On essence, the right and centre held a linear, Europe-centred view of civilisation, and Lai says this reduced "revolution" to a synonym for "democracy" and made socialists fellow travellers of capitalism. The left aimed at a new civilisation but fragmented, because spontaneity produced competing means and goals, each claiming to embody the essence.

Lai concludes that "revolution" must be grasped as a whole, drawing on Marx and Engels, with means, goals and essence corresponding to the subject, object and motive of revolution. Means must not be abstracted into "democracy", and essence must not be abstracted into slogans. Lai calls for a unified, advanced new-type proletarian party, and says socialism and capitalism stand in a relation of negation of the negation, not of earlier and later stages of civilisation. In this light the Party's self-reform and social revolution are presented as permanent themes. Read the original if you want a Chinese scholarly reading of Bernstein, Kautsky and Luxemburg on revolution, and its argument about revolution's internal balance.
quoteEn: Understanding of the concept of "revolution" must always proceed from the whole; narrowly clinging to any single element will dissolve socialist revolution itself.
quoteZh: 对“革命”概念的理解和认识始终应当从整体出发，偏狭地固守其中任何一个元素，都会消解社会主义革命本身。

glossary.explanation: A term prominent in Party discourse for the ruling party's continual internal renewal and correction of its own faults. The article links it with social revolution as a permanent task of proletarian parties.

t: New trends in the unification of communist parties worldwide in recent years and how China should respond
zh: 近年来世界共产党联合化新趋势与我们的应对
paras: Writing around the centenary of the Communist Party of China (2021), Yu Weihai asks what state the international communist movement is in amid what the article calls changes unseen in a century. Yu argues that the world's many communist and workers' parties show a clear tendency towards coordination. In Yu's account, this is a new historical pattern, different from the 19th- and 20th-century Internationals.

The article has four parts. It first describes how party unification shows itself: standing platforms, joint statements, coordinated protests and a shared ethos. It then identifies four new features, assesses the trend's effects, and ends with policy proposals for China. Yu draws on lists of international party forums, counts of joint statements, and the author's own 2019 field research in the United States.

Yu holds that the new unity rests on equal, voluntary association rather than a single centre, programme or line. It is plural, networked and organised around issues rather than organisations, and parties often belong to several platforms at once. Yu credits it with strengthening resistance to capitalism and showing that the international movement has not left the stage. Yu also stresses that sectarianism persists: the article cites some 400 communist parties worldwide, exclusionary forums and many factions, which Yu says leave unification inefficient. Diversity, in this view, adds cohesion but also breeds dogmatism and sharpens the tension between immediate and long-term goals.

For China, Yu proposes more research on the international movement and on Xi Jinping's idea of a "new type of party relations". Yu also urges strategic composure: China should not lead, carry the banner, join or oppose, since developing socialism with characteristics of Chinese characteristics is its greatest contribution. Yu warns that some foreign parties criticise China within joint statements, and adds that other parties' support, such as praise for China's pandemic response, can be used. Yu suggests united-front work, party-to-party dialogue led by the International Department and a national think tank. Read the original if you want a Chinese academic view of how communist party networks are assessed and how China's party diplomacy toward them is framed.
quoteEn: Developing the great cause of socialism with Chinese characteristics well is the greatest contribution to the international communist movement.
quoteZh: 认真发展好中国特色社会主义伟大事业，就是对国际共运的最大贡献。

glossary.explanation: A concept associated with Xi Jinping for the CPC's relations with foreign parties, stressing independence, equality, mutual respect and non-interference.
The worldwide movement of communist parties, from the Communist League and the Internationals onwards. Chinese texts abbreviate it as 国际共运.
The Party's practice of building alliances with and winning the support of groups outside the Party; here it is applied to foreign communist parties.

t: The idea of totality
st: From Hegel and Marx to the founders of Marxism outside China
zh: 总体性思想
zhSub: 从黑格尔、马克思到国外马克思主义的奠基者
source: Teaching and Research (Jiaoxue yu yanjiu), 2021 no. 6
paras: Yang Haifeng asks how the concept of totality passed from Hegel to Marx and then became the entry point through which Lukács, Korsch and Gramsci rethought Marxist philosophy. The article's thesis is that these three first-generation thinkers of foreign Marxism broke with the Second International tradition by recovering totality as the core of Marx's philosophy. Yang opens by noting that modern specialisation and the division of labour have blurred any picture of society as a whole, and that philosophy has repeatedly tried to restore one.

The text has three parts. The first traces totality in Hegel's account of the beginning of science as a circle, his critique of Kant's thing-in-itself and the dialectic of self-consciousness, and then in Marx's method in the 1857 Introduction. The second follows Lukács from Soul and Form and The Theory of the Novel through History and Class Consciousness to the late Ontology of Social Being. The third turns to Korsch (Marxism and Philosophy, Karl Marx) and Gramsci, and closes by comparing the three.

Yang argues that Marx kept Hegel's totality but changed its ground: totality is rooted in social being and its production and reproduction, not in spirit. In Yang's reading it is a mediated whole organised by a dominant relation, which under capitalism is capital. Marx also saw unbridgeable fractures in this whole, and Yang says Marx did not think reason could reconcile them. For Lukács, totality is both a dialectical method and an ideal state of social being. Reification, rationalisation and the antinomies of classical German philosophy express its absence, and the late work grounds it in labour. Korsch insists that philosophy, political economy and scientific socialism form one revolutionary theory, and that splitting them vulgarises Marxism. Gramsci treats Marxism as self-sufficient and 'organic', and reads hegemony as political, economic and cultural together, not as a purely cultural doctrine.

Yang concludes that the three thinkers revived Marxist philosophy against the mechanical Marxism of the Second International and brought the question of subjectivity into the discussion of totality. Their emphases differ. Lukács is the philosopher whose reification critique has strong purchase on reality. Korsch stresses the links between Marx's philosophy, political economy and socialism. Gramsci stresses the unity of politics, economy and culture. Yang adds that their work shaped the Frankfurt School and foreign Marxism from the 1930s to the 1960s. Read the original if you want a close account of how totality links Hegel, Marx and early Western Marxism, from a leading Chinese scholar of foreign Marxism.
quoteEn: The perspective of totality became Lukács's basic principle for examining problems.
quoteZh: 总体性视野成为卢卡奇考察问题的基本原则。

glossary.explanation: The Chinese academic label for Marxist currents developed outside China, including but broader than Western Marxism. It is a recognised research field in Chinese universities.
The international federation of socialist parties founded in 1889. The article uses it to name the orthodox, economistic reading of Marxism that Lukács, Korsch and Gramsci opposed.

Lukács's term in History and Class Consciousness for the way social relations take the form of relations between things under commodity production. Yang places it alongside Marx's commodity fetishism.
Gramsci's concept of leadership that combines political, economic and cultural dimensions. Yang argues it is often wrongly reduced to cultural hegemony.

t: Commemoration and reflection by the foreign left on the 200th anniversary of Engels's birth
zh: 国外左翼对恩格斯诞辰200周年的纪念与省思
source: Studies on Socialism (Shehui zhuyi yanjiu), 2021 no. 3
paras: Yuan Qun and Wang Enming survey how left-wing parties, organisations and scholars outside China marked the 200th anniversary of Engels's birth in 2020, and what they said about him. Their thesis is that these tributes defended Engels's standing against long-running attempts to set him against Marx, and showed his ideas still guide the world socialist movement as it moves, in the authors' words, from a low ebb towards revival.

The article first catalogues the commemorations: conferences in Portugal, Laos, Vietnam, Germany and Japan, joint declarations by Marxist-Leninist-Maoist parties, memorial essays by party leaders and academics, and events in Wuppertal and Moscow. It then groups the foreign left's assessments under four headings: Engels's historical position as Marx's indispensable 'second violin', the global significance of his works, their contemporary value, and the practical tasks the left drew from the anniversary.

In the authors' account, foreign left voices affirmed Engels as co-founder of Marxism and scientific socialism and as a leader of the international workers' movement. They credited him with contributions to philosophy, political economy, the theory of the family and state, and proletarian military science. The authors report that these voices rejected the 'Marx–Engels opposition' thesis and the claim that the late Engels abandoned revolution for parliamentarism. They also report that speakers read the Covid-19 pandemic, financial crises and growing wealth concentration as confirming his analysis of capitalism. Cited figures include Gennady Zyuganov, Sitaram Yechury and Brinda Karat, along with Vietnamese Party sources.

The authors conclude that the 2020 commemoration continued the 2018 Marx bicentenary and that Engels's theory of scientific socialism, workers' struggle and party-building remains relevant. They note the practical proposals the foreign left drew from it: building revolutionary parties, strengthening the study and publication of Marxist theory, and forming anti-war united fronts. They describe the commemorations, held amid what they call an intensifying imperialist anti-communist offensive, as a form of Marxist-Leninist education. Read the original if you want a detailed inventory of foreign left events, statements and sources on Engels in 2020, as reported from a Chinese academic perspective.
quoteEn: This commemoration was, moreover, a vivid practice of Marxist-Leninist education.
quoteZh: 这次纪念活动更是一场马列主义教育的生动实践。

t: An analysis of the reform of Vietnam's National Assembly oversight system since Đổi Mới
zh: 革新开放以来越南国会监督制度改革探析
paras: Since the launch of renovation and opening up (Đổi Mới) in 1986, how has Vietnam's National Assembly strengthened its supervision of state organs and officials, and what can China learn from it? Liu Yudi argues that Vietnam has steadily widened and refined National Assembly oversight in response to four concrete problems: the spread of bourgeois liberalization, corruption, uneven implementation of Party Central Committee decisions, and weak supervisory results. In Liu's account, over thirty years of reform have made oversight an indispensable part of the Party and state power-supervision system, although the problems have not been fully resolved.

The article is organised around those four problems, followed by a section of lessons for China. It traces changes in who may be questioned, reviewed or subjected to confidence votes, from 1986 through 2013 and beyond. It draws on cases such as the 2006 questioning of Prime Minister Phan Van Khai, the 2010 rejection of the north–south high-speed rail proposal, the Vinashin losses, and thematic supervision of education, higher education, land management and food safety. Liu also lists procedural innovations in questioning and report review from 2009 to 2019.

Liu presents the reforms as a response to the shock of the Soviet collapse and to liberal figures within the Party, who the author says promoted multi-party politics and the separation of powers. The Assembly removed such figures and then extended supervision to every body it elects or approves. Against corruption, it concentrated on senior leaders, using confidence votes and evaluations governed by a 2012 resolution, with the posts covered later narrowed to about fifty. To enforce Party decisions, it used thematic supervision teams that review reports, conduct field investigations, hold seminars and cooperate with ministries. To improve effectiveness, it introduced interactive formats such as grouped questions, live debate, one-minute questions and three-minute answers, and added procedural steps.

Liu concludes that socialist states should reform the supervision systems of their organs of state power while upholding the Marxist theory of the state and the laws of socialist democracy. Three lessons are drawn for China's National People's Congress: make fuller use of deputies' initiative, coordinate supervisory bodies and mechanisms into a joint force, and perfect mechanisms so that oversight becomes a sharp weapon against corruption. Read the original if you want a Chinese scholar's account of Vietnam's parliamentary oversight, with dated procedural details and the reform lessons it proposes for China.
quoteEn: People's deputies hold an important position in the supervisory activities of organs of state power, and their active role should be fully drawn out and exercised.
quoteZh: 人民代表在国家权力机关监督活动中具有重要地位，要充分挖掘和发挥人民代表的能动作用。

glossary.explanation: The Chinese rendering of Vietnam's Đổi Mới reform policy, adopted at the Communist Party of Vietnam's Sixth Congress in 1986. It introduced market mechanisms into a socialist framework.
A term used in Communist Party discourse for the promotion of Western-style multi-party politics, pluralism and rejection of Marxist guidance. Here it refers to such currents within Vietnam's Party.
A vote by which the National Assembly may express confidence in senior officials it elected or approved. It can lead to dismissal. It is preceded by a confidence evaluation.
A form of National Assembly oversight that examines how a particular policy or law has been implemented. It is carried out by dedicated teams through report review, field visits and seminars.
China's national legislature and, constitutionally, its highest organ of state power. Its deputies and Standing Committee have supervisory functions over the government, courts and procuratorates.

t: The dissemination of Marx's Capital in Germany
zh: 马克思《资本论》在德国的传播历程研究
source: Foreign Theoretical Trends (国外理论动态), 2021 no. 4
paras: Wang Zhan asks how Marx's Capital and its large body of manuscripts were spread and received in Germany, the country of Marx's birth and the language of his text. The article argues that this history, which forms part of the wider history of Marxism, shows two things. German scholars developed a double narrative, one revolutionary and one academic. German scholarship is also marked by rigorous philological work and philosophical speculation.

The study is chronological and has four parts. It covers the early dissemination under Marx and Engels from the 1860s to the 1890s, then popularisation from the 1890s to the 1930s. It then treats the publication of the manuscripts and the rise of the "New Reading of Marx" from 1930 to the 1990s, and finally developments since 2000. It draws on figures such as Engels, Karl Kautsky, David Riazanov, Henryk Grossmann, Friedrich Pollock, Hans-Georg Backhaus and Helmut Reichelt.

Wang first describes how Engels fought the bourgeois economists' "conspiracy of silence" after 1867 by writing reviews and a study outline. Engels also edited later German editions and Volumes II and III. Wang then follows the popular and abridged editions by Johann Most, Kautsky, Julian Borchardt and Kautsky's sons. The article notes criticisms of these editions, for example that Borchardt rearranged Marx's order and that the Kautskys' editions removed the description of workers' conditions and carried a reformist preface. It also covers Kautsky's edition of Theories of Surplus Value. In the middle sections Wang traces the MEGA1 and MEGA2 projects, the early Frankfurt School's readings of Capital, and the "New Reading of Marx". Grossmann read the three volumes as a methodological unfolding of accumulation and breakdown, Pollock stressed money theory, and Backhaus and Reichelt centred value-form theory and the dialectic.

Wang notes that MEGA2 Part II, completed in 2012, allows Marx's manuscripts and Engels's edited text to be compared line by line for the first time. Michael Heinrich is cited as saying that debate over Capital now has a sufficient textual basis. Since 2007 student reading campaigns, the Marx Autumn School and the Rosa Luxemburg Foundation's courses have brought Capital to wider German audiences, according to the article. Read the original if you want a detailed, source-based survey of the German publication history and editions of Capital and of the scholarly traditions around it.
quoteEn: The history of the dissemination of Capital and its body of manuscripts is an important part of the history of the dissemination of Marxism.
quoteZh: 《资本论》及其手稿群的传播史是马克思主义传播史的重要组成部分

t: Three dimensions of academic-history research on Western Marxism and their contemporary value
zh: 论西方马克思主义学术史研究的三个面向及其当代价值
source: Studies on the Marxist Theory Discipline (《马克思主义理论学科研究》), 2021 no. 8
paras: Wang Yuchen distinguishes the intellectual history of Western Marxism, which traces how the tradition developed, from its academic history, which builds on that record to examine the tradition's inner theoretical logic, its theoretical effects and its practical effects. The article argues that these three dimensions together structure academic-history research and that each carries value for the present.

The article has three sections. The first reconstructs the starting point and unfolding of Western Marxism's theoretical logic. The second assesses its theoretical effects on Marxism outside China, on later schools and on Chinese Marxist philosophy. The third turns to practical effects on Western socialist movements and new social movements. Figures discussed include Lukács, Korsch, Gramsci, Althusser, the Frankfurt School, Sartre, Lefebvre, Jameson, ecological Marxists and analytical Marxists.

For Wang, the tradition arose from reflection on failed Western revolutions and began with the question of what Marxist philosophy essentially is. Its thinkers rejected readings of Marxism as an early-modern, knowledge-theoretical philosophy. They stressed its critical and practical side and developed five lines of theory: alienation, cultural-ideological critique, critique of technological rationality, ecological critique and political philosophy. Wang then traces their effects. Post-Marxism borrowed from Gramsci and Althusser while, in Wang's account, distorting them. The late Marxism of Jameson and Eagleton and British cultural studies drew on the tradition more fruitfully. Wang describes foreign Marxism as making two turns, first to culture and then back to political economy. In practice, one strand sought the emancipation of the proletariat as a whole and the other that of the individual. Wang links the second strand to the 1968 student revolts and to ecological movements, and notes the limits of these theories, including subjectivising alienation and mixing up alienation with objectification.

Wang concludes that Western Marxism helped Chinese scholars understand the nature of Marxist philosophy. Since reform and opening up it has fed Chinese debates on practice, subjectivity and philosophical form, and has opened new fields such as cultural, technology-critical and ecological philosophy. Wang holds that these fields help address negative phenomena in China's modernization. Read the original if you want a Chinese scholar's systematic account of how Western Marxism is assessed and used in Chinese Marxist philosophy.
quoteEn: Western Marxism emerged as the result of reflection on the failure of Western revolutions.
quoteZh: 西方马克思主义的产生是对西方革命失败反思的结果。

glossary.explanation: The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in China in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.

t: The theoretical essence of Lenin's New Economic Policy and its contemporary value
zh: 列宁新经济政策的理论精髓及其当代价值
source: Contemporary World and Socialism (Dangdai shijie yu shehuizhuyi)
paras: Writing on the centenary of the New Economic Policy (NEP), Wang Jinfen and Yang Xiuqin ask what is essential in Lenin's turn of March 1921 from War Communism and why it still matters. They recall that Deng Xiaoping, thinking about what socialism is and how to build it, judged that Lenin's approach with the NEP was the better one, and that Xi Jinping praised the NEP in 2013 as the fruit of Lenin's arduous exploration without precedent. The authors argue that four elements of its theoretical essence offer lessons for socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era.

The article is organised around these four elements, each treated through Lenin's speeches and writings of 1920–22. They are: popular satisfaction as the basis of Party policy and the measure of its success; starting from practice rather than books; looking at problems politically and avoiding political dangers and errors; and using capitalism to build socialism. Each section ends by linking Lenin's position to statements by Xi Jinping and to present-day Party tasks.

In the authors' account, the Kronstadt sailors' revolt and the peasant uprisings and strikes of 1920–21 showed that War Communism, with grain requisitioning and the abolition of trade, had cut the Party's policy off from the people. Lenin therefore treated the people's will as decisive and demanded real economic work over empty talk. The authors say he broke with the conceptions of Marx and Engels, admitting that no book had dealt with state capitalism under communism. They present the NEP as above all a political question, namely the relationship between workers and peasants, resting on an economic union of the two. For this reason Lenin rejected Trotsky's separation of politics from economics and banned factions at the 10th Party Congress. On capitalism, the authors read Lenin as treating it as a necessary intermediate link between small-scale production and socialism, to be channelled into state capitalism. He also warned that Communists lacked the skill to steer it, likening the policy to a car that does not obey its driver, and urged them to out-compete the capitalists.

The authors conclude that Lenin's lessons apply today. In their view the Party should put the people's satisfaction first and treat Marxism as developing with practice. They also call for political awareness, sensitivity and judgement among cadres in a period of great global change, noting that some Party members still lack it. And they hold that China must learn from the achievements of capitalism while staying alert to capital's profit-seeking nature and to Western attempts at containment. They say China should neither return to a rigid, closed path nor change its banner. Read the original if you want a Chinese Party-scholarly reading of the NEP, with extensive Lenin quotations, as a guide to current policy on markets, capital and Party leadership.
quoteEn: Realising socialism is the fundamental purpose of the NEP's permitting capitalist elements to exist.
quoteZh: 实现社会主义是新经济政策允许资本主义因素存在的根本目的。

glossary.explanation: The policy adopted in Soviet Russia in 1921 to replace War Communism. It introduced a tax in kind on grain, allowed limited private trade and concessions to foreign capital, and restored money and commodity exchange.
The emergency economic system of 1918–21 during the Russian Civil War. It featured grain requisitioning, nationalised industry and a ban on private trade.
In Lenin's usage, capitalist enterprise such as concessions and leases operating under the control of the Soviet state. He saw it as a step towards socialism in a small-peasant country.
The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's path of socialist development since reform and opening up.

t: The Communist Party of Vietnam: setting out on a new journey through inheritance and upholding fundamentals
zh: 越南共产党：在传承与守正中踏上新征程
source: Report on the Development of the International Communist Movement (2020–2021), Social Sciences Academic Press, June 2021, pp. 143–165
paras: This chapter, from the Report on the Development of the International Communist Movement (2020–2021), reviews what the Communist Party of Vietnam did in 2020, the year before its 13th Congress. Pan and Wei argue that the Party combined two tasks: upholding Marxism-Leninism and Ho Chi Minh Thought through commemorations, and preparing leadership, documents and strategy for the Congress. In their account, this strengthened the Party's ruling position and public confidence amid ideological pressure and the Covid-19 pandemic.

The text has four parts. The first covers the 2020 anniversaries: the Party's 90th, Ho Chi Minh's 130th, Lenin's 150th and Engels's 200th, together with the campaign against hostile forces and what the authors call 'peaceful evolution'. The second examines the turnover of leadership at all levels and the selection of the 13th Central Committee. The third covers the drafting of the Congress documents, the assessment of 35 years of renovation (Đổi Mới) and the targets to 2045. The fourth offers an overall assessment and outlook for 2021.

The authors present the commemorations as a deliberate ideological strategy. Central Party directives classified and organised the events, and general secretary Nguyen Phu Trong described the Party's leadership as the decisive factor in all Vietnamese revolutionary victories. In the authors' reading, 'upholding fundamentals' is the root of inheritance and inheritance serves upholding fundamentals. On personnel, they describe detailed cadre standards, such as Regulation 214, and a staged selection process. Yet Trong's third term as general secretary came through a special procedure that bypassed the Party Charter's two-term limit. The authors explain this as a vote by the Congress, as the Charter's highest authority, after no other candidate won a majority of support, and they judge it favourable to continuity.

The authors credit the Party's centralised leadership with Vietnam's pandemic record and 2.91 per cent growth in 2020. They summarise the Congress targets: high-income developed status by 2045, with growth of 6.5–7 per cent a year in 2021–2025. They nonetheless judge the goals of escaping the middle-income trap and reaching high-income status hard to square with 2020 per-capita GDP of US$2,750 and the projected growth rates. They also note that a third Covid-19 wave in early 2021 may make the 6.5 per cent growth target difficult. Read the original if you want a detailed Chinese-scholarly account of Vietnamese Party documents, personnel procedures and ideological work around the 13th Congress.
quoteEn: Upholding fundamentals is the root of inheritance, and inheritance exists for the sake of upholding fundamentals.
quoteZh: 守正是传承之本，传承是为了守正。

glossary.explanation: A term used in communist-party discourse for alleged Western efforts to undermine socialist systems from within by non-military means such as ideological and cultural infiltration. The article uses it for the threat Vietnam's Party says it faces.

The reform policy launched by the Communist Party of Vietnam in 1986, moving the country towards a socialist-oriented market economy. The article treats 35 years of it as the basis of Party legitimacy.

The Communist Party of Vietnam's official guiding ideology alongside Marxism-Leninism. It is presented as the creative application of Marxism-Leninism to Vietnamese conditions, joining national independence with socialism.

t: The problem logic of Western Marxism and its contemporary value
zh: 论西方马克思主义的问题逻辑及当代价值
paras: Wang Yuchen asks how Chinese scholarship on Western Marxism can move beyond summarising individual thinkers' views to grasping the "problem logic" that organises the tradition. The article argues that this logic starts from a single question, whether the essence of Marxist philosophy lies in its specific conclusions or in a dialectic that unites theory and practice. Wang holds that grasping it helps clarify the tradition's substance and lets it serve as a resource for adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.

The article has four parts. It first traces the theoretical starting point, from Lukács, Korsch and Gramsci to the humanist and scientistic readings of Marx. It then examines Western Marxism's cultural and ideological critique of contemporary capitalism. A third part treats its theoretical innovations: alienation and everyday-life critique, critique of technical rationality, ecological critique and political philosophy. A final part assesses their contemporary effects and value for China.

Wang argues that the early Western Marxists rejected economic-determinist and natural-science readings of Marx, which they blamed for the failure of Western revolutions. They presented Marxism as a modern philosophy of practice centred on a critical, value-laden dialectic. Wang then divides the tradition into theories of the liberation of the proletariat as a whole (Lukács, Gramsci, Althusser, ecological and analytical Marxists) and theories of individual liberation (the Frankfurt School, Sartre). Both turned to culture and ideology, but the first aimed at class consciousness and political revolution, the second at autonomous personality through aesthetics and love. Wang credits the alienation theory with showing that material wealth brought control rather than freedom. Wang also criticises it for tracing alienation to technical rationality rather than private ownership and the division of labour, for treating it as a subjective experience, and for conflating objectification with alienation.

Wang concludes that the Western Marxist problem logic has broad value. It set Marx's philosophy apart from modern epistemology, and it opposed the Soviet "dialectical and historical materialism" textbook model. It also shaped urban, ecological and feminist movements, post-Marxism (which Wang says fell into subjective idealism) and the "late Marxism" of Eagleton, Jameson and Harvey, which Wang says returned to political economy. In China, Wang says, it prompted rethinking of the textbook system and of the relation between scholarship and practical relevance. It also opened work on cultural, everyday-life, technology, ecological and political philosophy relevant to the problems of modernity in China's modernization. Read the original if you want a Chinese scholar's systematic account and critique of Western Marxism's internal logic and of its reception in China.
quoteEn: The inquiry into the essence of Marxist philosophy is whether that essence lies in its specific conclusions or in a dialectic that unites theory and practice, and this forms the theoretical starting point of Western Marxism's problem logic.
quoteZh: 对马克思主义哲学本质的追问体现为马克思主义哲学的本质到底是其具体结论，还是“理论与实践相统一”的辩证法，这构成西方马克思主义问题逻辑的理论起点。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: Official formula for the Party's project of fitting Marxist theory to China's conditions and to present-day circumstances. The article uses the shorter 'Sinicization of Marxism'.
The tradition running from Lukács, Korsch and Gramsci through the Frankfurt School and Althusser. It is known for emphasis on philosophy, culture and ideology.

t: Infinite form and the spark of truth: the materialist dialectic in Badiou's The Immanence of Truths
zh: 无限形式与真理的星星之火——论巴迪欧《真理的内在性》中的唯物辩证法
paras: Lan Jiang reads Alain Badiou's 2018 book L'Immanence des vérités, which Badiou presents as the third volume of the Being and Event series, as the possible capstone of his philosophy. The article asks what happens to the finite world once a subject has touched the infinite through a truth procedure. Its thesis is that the book "turns the project around" and builds a new materialist dialectic. In it, finite objects are held to be immanent to truth rather than prior to it.

The article opens with Badiou's repeated use of Mao Zedong's phrase "a single spark can start a prairie fire" and his rewording of it in the new book. It then uses Plato's cave to frame the book's question, and sets Badiou's two philosophical manifestos (1989 and 2009) against postmodern and post-structuralist currents. The later sections cover Badiou's two opponents, transcendence and "democratic materialism", his appeal to set theory, and his treatment of the finite. Lan draws on Being and Event, Logics of Worlds, Wittgenstein, Deleuze and Meillassoux.

Lan argues that Badiou rewrites Mao's phrase so that the spark is no longer the cause of the prairie fire. It becomes a concrete flash thrown up by an omnipresent infinity. Fidelity to the spark therefore means fidelity to an event, not the manufacture of sparks. The new dialectic fights on two fronts. Against a transcendent One (God, Substance, Nature, Hegel's Absolute), Badiou follows Cantor in separating the infinite from the One, so that the infinite becomes a "multiple without one". Against democratic materialism, whose axiom is that "there are only bodies and languages", he holds that the finite is not given but is the result of an infinite operation of counting-as-one. Lan calls this finitude the central fetishistic ideology of our age.

Lan concludes that, for Badiou, liberation is a formal revolution. A new form, even one without objects, is created, subjects incorporate themselves into the generic set it opens, and objects take shape within it. This explains why Badiou privileges mathematics over physics and chemistry. Lan presents this as Badiou's new materialist dialectic and his way of picturing a future society, one that does not return to a primal One. Read the original if you work on Badiou, Marxist ontology or the French reception of Mao, and want a close account of how The Immanence of Truths connects set theory, the critique of finitude and the image of the spark.
quoteEn: In Badiou's view, the aim of philosophy cannot be to stay silent about the unsayable as Wittgenstein does. It is to create a form, to create generic procedures of truth, so that what could not be said can appear under a new form.
quoteZh: 巴迪欧认为,哲学的目的当然不能像维特根斯坦那样对不可言说的保持沉默,而是我们要创造一种形式,创造出真理的类性程序,让原本不能言说的东西可以在新的形式下呈现出来。

glossary.explanation: Badiou's term, from Logics of Worlds, for the contemporary outlook that recognises only bodies and languages and denies truths and the infinite. The article treats it as one of the two enemies of the new materialist dialectic.
A concept from Badiou's Being and Event. A structure that presents the pure multiple as unified objects, so that the "one" is an operation rather than something given.

t: Four paths in contemporary French Marxist research and their assessment
zh: 当代法国马克思主义研究的四条路径及其评析
paras: Chinese scholarship on French Marxism has traditionally concentrated on Althusser, Sartre and Lefebvre, all now dead. Cheng asks what research paradigms exist in French Marxism today, how they develop and how they relate to one another. The article argues that contemporary French Marxism is best understood as Marxism in the post-Althusser era, whose four main paths share a common logic of emancipatory politics while each carrying theoretical weaknesses.

The article examines four representatives in turn: Jacques Bidet, Alain Badiou, Jacques Rancière and Étienne Balibar. Each section introduces the thinker's career and then reconstructs one paradigm: Bidet's meta-structure theory built on a reading of Capital, Badiou's philosophy of the event aimed at communism, Rancière's politics of literature and aesthetics organised around equality, and Balibar's work on race and nation, which Cheng labels post-Marxist. A concluding section compares the four with Althusser's legacy and with one another.

In Cheng's account, Bidet finds in Marx a double logic of market and organisation, with law logically prior to production. From it he derives a ruling class composed of owners of capital and holders of organisational and knowledge-based competence, opposed to the popular classes. Badiou distinguishes two kinds of politics and holds that an unpredictable event ruptures the existing order and calls a subject into being, so that truth takes the form of the idea of communism. Rancière separates "police" from "politics" and treats politics as the appearance of those with no part, then turns to literature as a way of making the unseen visible. Balibar moves from structuralist Marxism to ambiguous race–nation–class identities and then to "equaliberty", the mutual implication of equality and freedom.

Cheng concludes that all four thinkers are tied to Althusser, whether by inheritance (Balibar, Bidet), rebellion (Rancière) or the notion of rupture (Badiou), and that Balibar, Rancière and Badiou share an emancipatory politics for the masses, while Bidet seeks socialism through an alliance of the masses with organisational competence. The weaknesses Cheng names are the risk of wordplay and tautology in equaliberty, the unresolved realities of transnational politics, and, for Rancière and Badiou, a utopian quality and the loss of a historical-materialist foundation. Cheng sees Bidet and Balibar as more grounded in social reality, and Rancière and Badiou as preachers of ideas. Read the original if you want a Chinese scholar's map of post-Althusser French Marxism and a critical assessment of these four thinkers from a historical-materialist standpoint.
quoteEn: The logic of emancipatory politics runs through the thought of Balibar, Rancière and Badiou from beginning to end.
quoteZh: 解放政治的逻辑贯穿于巴里巴尔、朗西埃、巴迪欧思想的始终

t: Commemoration and reflection by the foreign left on the 200th anniversary of Engels's birth
zh: 国外左翼对恩格斯诞辰200周年的纪念与省思
paras: Yuan Qun and Wang Enming survey how left-wing parties, organisations and scholars outside China marked the bicentenary of Friedrich Engels's birth in 2020. They argue that these commemorations defended Engels's standing against long-running disparagement and showed that his thought still guides the world socialist movement as it moves, in the authors' words, from a low ebb towards revival.

The article opens with a catalogue of events: conferences in Lisbon, Hanoi, Vientiane and Japan, joint declarations by Marxist-Leninist-Maoist parties, commemorative articles by figures such as Gennady Zyuganov, Brinda Karat, Marcello Musto and Michael Roberts, and a 'Engels Year' in Wuppertal. It then reviews what these sources say about Engels's historical position, his contributions to philosophy, political economy, scientific socialism and military science, and the present-day value of his ideas. It closes with the strategies the left drew from the anniversary.

The authors argue first that foreign leftists reject historical nihilism and affirm Engels as co-founder of Marxism and a leader of the workers' movement, the irreplaceable 'second violin' beside Marx. Second, they report that these writers answer the claims that Marx and Engels were opposed, or that the late Engels abandoned revolution for parliamentarism, by treating his work as a living weapon. Cited examples include his analysis of capital concentration, said to be borne out by the global financial crisis and the Covid-19 pandemic, and his account of women's oppression in The Origin of the Family, Private Property and the State.

The authors conclude that the commemorations continued the 2018 Marx bicentenary and showed Engels's theory to be still relevant to class liberation. They report three practical lessons drawn abroad: building revolutionary proletarian parties, strengthening the study and publication of Marxist theory, and forming broad anti-war and workers' fronts. They add that the left's position in the heartland of imperialism gave its reading of Engels, in their view, both revolutionary optimism and sober realism. Read the original if you want a detailed, source-referenced map of foreign communist and left commemorations of Engels in 2020, including Vietnamese, Indian, Russian and European material, as seen from a Chinese academic viewpoint.
quoteEn: While paying tribute to one of history's great thinkers, the foreign left's commemoration and reflection on Engels strengthens its faith in the scientific truth of Marxism and actively considers strategies to move world socialism from its low ebb towards revival.
quoteZh: 国外左翼对恩格斯的纪念与省思，在向人类历史上伟大的思想家致敬的同时，坚定马克思主义科学真理的信念57，积极思考推动世界社会主义从低潮逐渐走向振兴的战略策略。

t: A critique of nature-centred ecological views and the construction of a new ecological philosophy
st: Reading Slavoj Žižek on ecology
zh: 自然中心主义生态观的批判与新生态哲学的建构
source: Foreign Social Sciences (Guowai shehui kexue), 2021 no. 2
paras: Why has the ecological crisis not eased despite decades of Western reflection on it? Shi Fengge argues that the weakness of "nature-centrism" (ziran zhongxinzhuyi) lies in its ontological premise: a perfectly balanced, pristine original nature that humans later damaged. Drawing on Slavoj Žižek, the article calls this premise a utopia and presents Žižek's alternative, a "new ecological philosophy" built on psychoanalysis.

The article has four parts. It first reconstructs the nature-centred outlook through three currents: ecological ethics (Schweitzer, Leopold, Rolston, with Barry Commoner's ecological law that nature knows best), wilderness philosophy, and Arne Naess's deep ecology. It then sets out Žižek's critique, mainly from In Defense of Lost Causes. Next it explains the new ecological philosophy's two components, the "future perfect" and collective action. A conclusion compares Žižek with Marx and Engels.

Shi's core argument is that, for Žižek, "nature does not exist". Nature is inherently catastrophic and unbalanced, as shown by a reading of Darwin in which evolution is clumsy improvisation, and by the claim that 90 per cent of the human genome is "junk" DNA. Since humans appeared it has also been a "second nature", and genetic technology deepens this. Žižek's response is a time-view in which disaster is treated as inevitable so that action can retroactively change what was possible, together with collective action. The latter is spelled out by reworking Badiou's four moments of the eternal Idea of justice: strict egalitarian justice, terror against violators of environmental rules, voluntarism, and trust in the people, including the figure of the informer. Shi presents this as a response to the "choice deadlock" of unknown unknowns.

Shi concludes that Žižek moves the ecological question from a utopian beyond to the practical problem of solving it, while grounding action in human value. The article finds links to Marx's view of nature as humanised and socially historical, to Engels's warning that nature takes revenge on human victories, and to Marx's concept of practice. It admits the new philosophy is imperfect but calls it a new perspective and path for global ecological problems. Read the original if you want a Chinese Marxist reading of Žižek's ecological thought, and of how it is set against deep ecology and Marx and Engels.
quoteEn: The future perfect is the fundamental attitude we should hold toward ecological problems, and the precondition on which we carry out collective action.
quoteZh: 先将来时是我们面对生态问题时所应持有的根本态度，是我们据以进行集体行动的前提。

glossary.explanation: A label for ecological views that give nature intrinsic value and rights against human-centred outlooks. The article applies it to ecological ethics, wilderness philosophy and deep ecology.

A tense (the French futur antérieur) used by Žižek for a time-view that looks back at the present from an imagined future. Treating catastrophe as certain is meant to prompt action that changes the past's possibilities.

The world shaped by human activity and social processes, as opposed to untouched nature. The article links Žižek's use of it to Marx's view that the sensuous world is a product of history and industry.
An ecological philosophy associated with Arne Naess. It stresses ecocentric equality and a wider ecological self that is realised together with other beings.

t: The idea of totality: from Hegel and Marx to the founders of Marxism outside China
zh: 总体性思想：从黑格尔、马克思到国外马克思主义的奠基者
source: Teaching and Research (Jiaoxue yu yanjiu), 2021 no. 6
paras: Modern specialisation and the division of labour have blurred the picture of society and the world as a whole. Yang Haifeng asks how the idea of totality, traced from Hegel through Marx, became the entry point by which Lukács, Korsch and Gramsci reread Marx's philosophy. Yang argues that this move broke with the research tradition of the Second International and founded the tradition of foreign Marxism.

The article has three parts. The first compares Hegel's and Marx's conceptions of totality. The second follows Lukács from his early works, Soul and Form and The Theory of the Novel, through History and Class Consciousness to his late Ontology of Social Being. The third turns to Korsch (Marxism and Philosophy, Karl Marx) and Gramsci (the Prison Notebooks), and closes by comparing the three.

Yang first shows how Hegel's totality is a mediated circle in which beginning and end coincide, and how Marx keeps this idea in his Grundrisse method. For Marx, a concrete thing is a unity of many determinations, and capital is the dominant relation that organises capitalist society. Yang then lists four differences: Marx grounds totality in social existence rather than spirit; he treats concepts as reflecting real development; he identifies capital as the true starting point and end point; and he sees irreparable fissures in capitalism that reason cannot reconcile. Lukács then uses totality both as a method (isolated facts only count as knowledge when grasped within a whole) and as an ideal state. From that ideal he criticises reification and the antinomies of bourgeois thought. Korsch and Gramsci stress the unity of Marxism's parts: philosophy, political economy and socialism for Korsch; philosophy, economics and politics for Gramsci, whose theory of hegemony Yang reads as political, economic and cultural together rather than merely cultural.

Yang concludes that the three thinkers seized the most important content of Marxist philosophy, the totalising study of social life. In doing so they helped remove the mechanical Marxism of the Second International and restored its vitality. Yang notes their differences: Lukács is the radical philosopher, Korsch the theorist of the links among Marxism's components, and Gramsci the revolutionary rooted in Italian reality. Their work, Yang says, directly shaped the Frankfurt School in the 1930s–60s. Read the original if you want a close account of how the concept of totality links Hegel, Marx and the first generation of Western Marxist thinkers, as seen by a leading Chinese scholar of foreign Marxism.
quoteEn: Together the three restored and reconstructed the theory of totality in Marxist philosophy, thereby forming a line of thought distinct from the orthodox research of the time and exerting a fairly far-reaching influence on later thinkers.
quoteZh: 他们三人共同恢复和重构了马克思主义哲学的总体性理论，从而形成了不同于当时正统研究的另一种思路，对后来者产生了较为深远的影响

glossary.explanation: A Chinese academic field covering Marxist thought developed outside China. It is broader than 'Western Marxism', which names the specific tradition of Lukács, Korsch, Gramsci and the Frankfurt School.

The idea that social life and knowledge form a mediated whole in which every element is understood through its place in the structure. It runs from Hegel through Marx and became central to Lukács and later Western Marxism.
Lukács's term for the way social relations among people appear as relations among things under commodity production. He built it on Marx's commodity fetishism, together with Simmel and Weber.
Gramsci's concept of leadership by consent, which Yang reads as political, economic and cultural at once.
The international federation of socialist parties (1889–1914). Its Marxism is often criticised in this literature as mechanical and economistic.

t: The successful experience of the Communist Party of China is a precious asset for the world
zh: 中国共产党的成功经验是世界宝贵财富
paras: This is a Chinese translation of a commentary by Ivan Melnikov, a Russian Communist Party leader and First Deputy Chairman of the State Duma, written for the centenary of the Communist Party of China in 2021. Melnikov argues that the Party's hundred years of leading revolution, construction and reform have produced experience that is a valuable asset for the whole world. He presents the Party as the force that restarted the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The piece follows the Party's history in broad stages. It begins with China's decline into a semi-colonial, semi-feudal society after 1840 and the spread of Marxism after the October Revolution. It then covers the founding of the Party in 1921 and the victory in the wars of liberation. Next come the building of the People's Republic after 1949, reform and opening up from 1978, and the period since Xi Jinping became General Secretary in 2012. The last part turns to Russian–Chinese relations.

Melnikov's core claim is that the Party's record in solving national problems explains its authority. He cites the creation of a complete national economic system by 1978 and rising literacy and life expectancy. He also cites China's share of world GDP, which he gives as 1.8 per cent in 1978 and close to 10 per cent by 2010, when China became the second-largest economy. For the period since 2012, he points to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and the Belt and Road Initiative. In his account, the Party now helps address global challenges and promotes progress, cooperation and humanitarianism.

Melnikov describes Russian–Chinese relations as the best in history. He bases this on the 2001 Treaty of Good-Neighbourliness and Friendly Cooperation, on cooperation between parties and legislatures, and on friendship societies and cultural exchange. He expresses confidence that firm adherence to the Party's line will bring new achievements. He adds that China's success gives the international communist movement more arguments for the promise of its aims, and that peoples on every continent will draw on the Party's experience. Read the original if you want an example of how a Russian communist politician framed the Party's centenary for a Chinese readership, including its emphasis on Sino-Russian ties.
quoteEn: The outstanding experience the Communist Party of China has accumulated over 100 years of leading China's revolution and socialist construction is a precious asset of the world today.
quoteZh: 中国共产党在领导中国革命和社会主义建设的100年间积累起来的杰出经验是当今宝贵的世界财富。

glossary.explanation: The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched at the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee in December 1978.
An international economic cooperation initiative proposed by Xi Jinping in 2013, evoking the ancient Silk Road, with infrastructure and trade links across Eurasia, Africa and beyond.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's guiding ideology associated with Xi Jinping. It was written into the Party constitution in 2017 and the state constitution in 2018.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A national goal in Party discourse, framed as restoring China's strength and standing after the 'century of humiliation' that began in 1840.

t: The Communist Party of Vietnam's theoretical exploration of socialist construction since Doi Moi
zh: 革新以来越南共产党对社会主义建设的理论探索
paras: Writing after the 13th Congress of the Communist Party of Vietnam (CPV) in 2021, Yan Jiehua asks how the party has developed its theory of socialist construction during 35 years of renovation (Doi Moi, begun in 1986). The article argues that this exploration has advanced along three lines: the theory of developmental stages in the socialist transition period, the theory of socialist democracy, and the theory of party building. Yan treats these as the CPV's attempt to combine Marxist principles with Vietnamese conditions, and aims to draw lessons for other socialist countries.

The article has three main sections, one for each line of theory. The first traces how the CPV's understanding of the transition period developed from the Sixth Congress (1986) through the Twelfth (2016) to the Thirteenth. The second follows the democracy formula, the relationships the party must handle, and the institutions built around it. The third covers party building, including the status of the political system and of cadre work. Yan draws heavily on congress documents and on statements by Nguyen Phu Trong and CPV theorists.

On the transition period, Yan argues that the Sixth Congress formed the theory, later congresses tied its stages to industrialization and modernization, and the Thirteenth Congress set new benchmarks. These benchmarks combine overall development level, industrial level and income level, with goals for 2025, 2030 and 2045. On democracy, Yan reads the move from a four-part formula to a six-part one as a step towards a state of law that belongs to, comes from and serves the people. The six parts are people know, discuss, do, inspect, supervise and enjoy, and the Thirteenth Congress added supervision and enjoyment. Yan notes that the formula was institutionalised through party directives, government decrees and National Assembly ordinances on grassroots democracy. On party building, the Thirteenth Congress made building a clean, strong political system a theme alongside party building. It also called cadre work the 'key of keys' and described a five-part pattern: politics, ideology, ethics, organisation and cadres.

Yan concludes that significant theoretical problems remain open. CPV theorists admit that the length of the transition period and the number of its stages are unresolved, and that it is unclear whether reaching high-income status in 2045 would end it. Some Vietnamese scholars doubt the new targets, since the goal of becoming a basically industrialised country by 2020 was not met. Yan also notes unresolved questions about the relation between democracy and discipline within democratic centralism, and acknowledges weaknesses in ideological work and in theoretical summing-up. Read the original if you want a Chinese scholar's overview of how Vietnam's ruling party has framed its post-1986 theory, with detailed references to CPV congress documents and official regulations.
quoteEn: The Thirteenth Congress used the criteria of 'overall development level, industrial level and income level' to redefine Vietnam's three key future stages, and the CPV holds that this standard is more scientific and better fits Vietnam's reality.
quoteZh: 越共十三大依据“综合发展水平、工业水平和收入水平”的标准重新确定了越南未来三个重要的发展阶段，越共认为这一标准更为科学，也更符合越南实际。

glossary.explanation: The reform programme the Communist Party of Vietnam launched at its Sixth Congress in 1986. It introduced market-oriented economic changes while keeping one-party rule.

In the Marxist-Leninist account, the long period between capitalism and a fully developed socialism. The CPV holds that Vietnam, which moved from small-scale production without a capitalist stage, is within this period.

glossary.zh: 民知、民议、民为、民检、民监、民享
glossary.pinyin: mín zhī, mín yì, mín wéi, mín jiǎn, mín jiān, mín xiǎng
glossary.en: people know, discuss, do, inspect, supervise and enjoy
glossary.explanation: The CPV's formula for popular participation. It started as 'people know, discuss, do, inspect' in 1986, and the Thirteenth Congress (2021) added supervision and enjoyment.
The Leninist organisational principle of free discussion followed by binding, disciplined unity in action. It governs Communist parties' internal life.
The CPV's phrase for the central importance of cadre work in party building, used in Thirteenth Congress documents.

t: The collapse of neoliberal myths and the direction of Western capitalism's evolution
zh: 新自由主义迷思的破灭与西方资本主义的演变方向
source: Ideological and Theoretical Education Herald (思想理论教育导刊), 2020 no. 11
paras: Writing in 2020, Wang Pengquan asks what the Western response to COVID-19 reveals about neoliberalism and where Western capitalism is heading. The article argues that neoliberalism survived the 2008 financial crisis and even intensified, but that the pandemic has now exposed its inner flaws and broken its main myths. In Wang's view this makes a transformation of Western capitalism urgent.

The article first sketches neoliberalism's rise after the Keynesian order broke down in the 1960s and 1970s. It then takes three myths in turn: market fundamentalism, extreme individualism and the illusion of "common prosperity" under capitalism. The evidence comes mainly from the United States and Europe, and Wang draws on Henry Giroux, Noam Chomsky, Jeremy Gilbert and others. A final section sets out three expected features of capitalism's evolution.

Wang argues that decades of privatisation, austerity and deregulation hollowed out public health systems and medical supply capacity, so that the claim that markets outperform the state failed in the pandemic. Extreme individualism, in this account, serves to blame individuals for failures of the system and to dissolve the collective solidarity that could resist capital. Citing wage, household-finance, unemployment and racial-disparity figures, the article contends that the 2008 bailouts deepened inequality and that the pandemic fell hardest on workers and ethnic minorities. Wang then predicts that capitalism will change faster, rebalancing government, capital and society. Left-wing thought and movements will gain influence, and non-Western experience, above all China's, will become a reference point.

Wang concludes that the pandemic confirms the "two inevitables" of Marxism, namely that capitalism will perish and socialism will triumph, and calls for stronger the Four-sphere Confidence. The author also urges close attention to how Western capitalism changes, so that positive elements can be used to build a community with a shared future for mankind and risks to China's external environment can be averted. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese Marxist scholar read the pandemic as the end of neoliberal legitimacy and drew conclusions about Western capitalism's course.
quoteEn: If the 2008 international financial crisis sounded the alarm bell for neoliberalism, then the multiple predicaments caused by the inadequate pandemic response of Western countries can be said to have sounded its death knell.
quoteZh: 如果说2008年国际金融危机敲响了新自由主义的警钟，那么此次西方国家疫情应对不足导致多重困境，可以说敲响了新自由主义的丧钟。

glossary.explanation: A formula from the Party leadership of the 2010s calling for confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy and theoretical concept associated with Xi Jinping, presented as a vision of international cooperation and shared development.
Shorthand for the Marxist claim, drawn from the Communist Manifesto, that capitalism will inevitably perish and socialism will inevitably triumph.

t: Europe's reshaping in the post-pandemic era and the strategy of the Left
zh: 后疫情时代的欧洲重塑与左翼战略
source: Frontiers of Foreign Social Sciences (国外社会科学前沿), 2021 no. 6 (excerpt)
paras: This text is a Chinese translation of an article by the Austrian economist Walter Baier, a former chair of the Austrian Communist Party and coordinator of the European left network Transform! Europe. Written in 2020, it asks what the Covid-19 crisis means for European integration and what strategy the European Left should adopt. Baier argues that the pandemic did not cause but accelerated the factors that will shape global development, including the end of unilateral US hegemony. He holds that it exposed structural flaws in the EU and that the Left must use the crisis to contest social hegemony.

The article has five parts. It begins with the EU's failed pandemic response, then turns to the coming recession, debt and the left's economic options. It next traces the conflict between market integration and democratic, politically planned integration from the 1951 Coal and Steel Community to Greece in 2015. Later sections cover Brexit and the limits of EU-centred pan-Europeanism, and Europe's place in the world, including relations with the United States, Russia and China.

Baier contends that EU treaties require member states to maintain social and health systems while the Stability and Growth Pact limits their finances. In his account, integration has advanced mainly through the market, from the Single European Act to the Maastricht and Lisbon treaties, and has repeatedly overridden democratic and social aims. He argues that the debt burden will deepen inequality between strong and weak states. He proposes abolishing the Pact, using the ECB, the European Investment Bank and the European Stability Mechanism to fund national social and ecological programmes, and imposing capital controls and taxes on wealth and capital gains. He also calls for putting banking and finance under social ownership, rather than relying on austerity and privatisation. He treats the nation state as the Left's basic source of strength and calls for a sovereign, freely elected European Parliament to replace the European Council as the EU's decision-making centre.

Baier concludes that Europe should reject a hostile, US-aligned stance towards China, which he notes is the EU's largest trading partner, and should treat cooperation with China as an opportunity. He adds that the European Left, which he says cannot fully endorse China's ideological model, should still work to rebuild international cooperation structures and reduce the risk of nuclear arms races. He presents the opening created by the crisis as temporary, lasting only until Europe's ruling classes reach a consensus. Read the original if you want a democratic-socialist European perspective on EU integration, debt and the post-pandemic order, published in a Chinese foreign-Marxism outlet.
quoteEn: The only way to overcome the deadlock is to extend democratic principles to every level of decision-making.
quoteZh: 克服僵局的唯一方法是使民主原则扩散到各级决策

t: Characteristics and development trends of the American left in the post-crisis era
zh: 论后危机时代美国左翼思潮的特征及发展趋势
source: Studies on Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping Theory, 2020 no. 7
paras: Pei Shaohua asks what marks left-wing thought in the United States after the 2008 financial crisis and where it is heading. Writing in 2020, Pei treats the crisis as an outbreak of capitalism's inherent contradictions and in essence a crisis of the capitalist system. The article argues that the American left is becoming more varied, more oriented towards practice and more favourable to socialism. Pei also holds that its pragmatist cultural roots limit it, and that it needs Marxist theory, a strong party and thorough revolution.

The article has three parts. The first identifies three features of the post-crisis American left, drawing mainly on the annual New York left forum. The second traces the cultural roots of this thought to American pragmatism, citing James, Peirce and Dewey and the forum's yearly themes from 2013 to 2019. The third sets out development trends, using the history of American socialism and passages from Marx, Engels and Lenin.

On the three features, Pei says eco-socialism, democratic socialism, feminist socialism and Marxism overlap and converge, because each answers the crisis and most point towards socialism. Pei calls democratic socialism a form of the 'petty-bourgeois socialism' that Marx and Engels criticised. Groups at the forum are also trying to turn ideas into action by forming an independent left party, and Bernie Sanders's 2016 campaign is cited as reviving interest in socialism. Pei argues that pragmatism's 'what is useful is true' outlook shapes these demands. It treats ideas as instruments and practice as isolated individual acts, so the left's aims are unlikely to be met given its unclear aims, disunited theory and uncoordinated action.

Pei concludes that the American left must be guided by Marxist theory, build a 'strong party' that truly represents the proletariat, and carry out thorough revolution. Pei rejects the hope of change through peaceful movements and elections, citing the suppression of Occupy Wall Street. The article cites a survey in which 40 per cent of Americans would prefer to live in a socialist country, and reads this as a favourable sign. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese Marxist scholar assesses the US left, using the New York left forum as evidence, and where Pei thinks it falls short.
quoteEn: Without thorough revolution, the American socialist movement cannot achieve final victory.
quoteZh: 不进行彻底的革命，美国的社会主义运动就不可能取得最终胜利。

t: Setbacks and reorganisation: a study of South Korean left-wing currents in the twenty-first century
zh: 挫折与重组:21世纪韩国左翼思潮研究
source: Foreign Theoretical Trends (国外理论动态), 2020 no. 2
paras: Jiao Pei asks how left-wing thought in South Korea has been reorganised since 2000, after the setbacks that followed the collapse of the Soviet bloc and the Asian financial crisis. The article, published in 2020, treats South Korea as a representative case of a medium-sized, late-developing, export-oriented capitalist country with a Confucian cultural background. Jiao argues that neoliberal reform produced new contradictions, and that left currents regrouped around them, with radical currents likely to fade and Marxist theory likely to regain attention.

The article has three parts. The first describes two features of Korean capitalism after 1997: 'monopoly under freedom' and 'extreme poverty amid prosperity'. The second surveys four currents: Trotskyism, 'liquidationism', the New Left and basic income theory, each tied to a representative scholar and to protest movements. The third forecasts the left's future under artificial intelligence and trade protectionism. Jiao relies on Korean statistics on employment, concentration, household debt and welfare spending.

On the economy, Jiao argues that deregulation after 1998 strengthened the chaebol rather than weakening them. Easier dismissal and agency labour fragmented workers, and the article cites figures on youth employment, temporary work and the 40 per cent share of irregular workers in 57 large firms in 2017. Jiao presents the four currents as responses to these conditions. Trotskyism, represented by Jung Seong-jin, holds that crisis is unavoidable and calls for a break with the bourgeoisie. Liquidationism, represented by Lee Jin-kyung, rejects Soviet socialism and proposes 'communalism'; Jiao calls it utopian and destructive without construction. The New Left, represented by Cho Dae-yeop and Jung Chul-hee, replaces class analysis with civil-society movements; Jiao says it is broad but struggles to move beyond joint demonstrations. Basic income theory, represented by Kang Nam-hoon, is presented as the most concrete programme, with the 2018 Child Allowance Act as a first step.

Jiao concludes that Trotskyism and liquidationism will fade as AI marginalises simple labour and protectionism weakens international labour cooperation. The New Left will deepen its work in feminist, environmental, disability and sexual-minority fields. Jiao expects the theory and method of scientific socialism to regain importance, pointing to the Korean translation of the Marx–Engels collected works from 2012. Jiao ends with the image of the traditional labour movement as the tide, the new movements as waves and the AI-driven technological revolution as a whirlpool. Read the original if you want a detailed Chinese-language survey of Korean left currents, with Korean data and names, written from within Chinese Marxist scholarship.
quoteEn: In sum, Korean liquidationism criticises Marxism in both methodology and theoretical content, trying to link West and East in space and the modern and the postmodern in time, and puts forward a communalist scheme with a utopian colouring.
quoteZh: 总之，韩国的清算主义主张从方法论和理论内容两个方面批判马克思主义，试图在空间上打通西方与东方，在时间上连接现代与后现代，提出了一个具有空想主义色彩的公社主义方案。

glossary.explanation: In this article, a Korean left current that rejects Soviet socialism and the theory of permanent revolution and draws on post-Marxism and postmodernism. The author distinguishes it from the broader Korean political practice of 'settling accounts' with opponents.

Here, a Korean current that moves beyond labour struggle to civil-society movements on gender, environment and human rights. It draws on Western Marxism and post-Marxism and sets aside class analysis.
The proposal that every member of society receive an unconditional income. The article presents it as an offshoot of the New Left in Korea, associated with Philippe Van Parijs.
The term for Marx and Engels's theory of socialism, as distinct from 'utopian' socialism. Chinese scholarship uses it for the core principles of Marxism.
The large family-controlled conglomerates, such as Samsung and Hyundai, that dominate the South Korean economy.

t: Recent developments in radical left social movements in Europe and the United States
zh: 当前欧美激进左翼社会运动的发展动态
source: International Studies Reference (Guoji yanjiu cankao), 2021 no. 5
paras: Writing in 2021, Li Xiaoling asks why radical left social movements in Europe and the United States have surged since the 2008 financial crisis, what marks them, and why they achieve so little. The article argues that explosive inequality under neoliberal finance-monopoly capitalism fuels the protests. In Li's view, the movements are held back by right-wing pressure, internal division and loose organisation, and their most viable path is a pan-left united front led by the working class.

The article has four parts. It begins with the background of inequality, using US data on income shares, the pandemic-era growth of billionaire wealth, and European figures on income growth, poverty and exclusion. It then surveys the movements themselves: Occupy Wall Street, the 2017 women's marches, the George Floyd protests, European anti-austerity strikes, and the "yellow vests" in France. A third part sets out the obstacles, and a fourth the likely direction of development.

Li identifies three features of the movements: frequent, large and widely spreading protests; a plural range of participants and demands; and networked mobilisation through social media. The author argues that class discourse (Greek strikes, US teachers' strikes) now coexists with identity discourse (Black Lives Matter, #MeToo), after the earlier "new social movements" had moved away from class struggle. Li then explains the constraints. Right-wing populism is in the ascendant, citing the defeats of Corbyn, Tsipras and Sanders, and left parties have drifted from the working class since the "Third Way". The movements also lack a unifying Marxist ideology, are non-violent and organised only loosely online, and offer no constructive alternative to neoliberalism.

Li concludes that movements confined to narrow issues or street protest cannot change the existing order. The author calls for a pan-left united front led by the working class, which is described as a large, internally stratified group of wage earners swelled by the "re-proletarianisation" of the middle class. It would ally with groups subject to special oppression, such as women, ethnic minorities, LGBTQ people and the disabled, and would need class consciousness built through workers' struggles. Li holds that the historical trend towards socialism replacing capitalism will not change. Read the original if you want a Chinese Marxist academic reading of Western left protest, with data, case examples and a view on the left's strategic prospects.
quoteEn: The seemingly surging wave of protest is in fact a heap of loose sand that cannot withstand wind and rain, and has failed to build consensus in adversity and form an irresistible revolutionary political force.
quoteZh: 看似汹涌澎湃的抗议浪潮实则是一盘经不起风吹雨打的散沙，未能在困境中凝聚共识形成一股锐不可当的革命性政治力量。

glossary.explanation: A broad alliance of working-class organisations and other progressive or oppressed groups against capitalism. The article proposes it as the strategy for the Western left.
A Marxist term for capitalism dominated by large financial and monopoly firms. The article uses it to describe the present Western system.
The claim that economic crisis pushes middle-class people into the position of wage-dependent workers, enlarging the proletariat.
Movements since the 1960s focused on gender, race, ecology and identity rather than class struggle and material welfare.

t: The contemporary reconstruction of Marx's category of "general intellect" and an assessment of its effects
zh: 马克思“一般智力”范畴的当代重构及其效应评估
source: Exploration and Contention (Tansuo yu zhengming), 2021 no. 1
paras: Sun Leqiang asks how contemporary Western left thinkers have redefined Marx's category of "general intellect", what theoretical system they built on it, and how that system should be judged. The article, published in 2021, argues that Italian autonomism and the cognitive capitalism school turned a category tied to fixed capital into a generalised property of living subjects. In Sun's assessment, this move narrows and at the same time inflates Marx's concept, and ends in a "fetishism" of general intellect.

The article has three parts. The first follows Paolo Virno's shift from "general intellect" to "intellect in general", together with its consequences for the labour theory of value, "real abstraction" and fixed capital (via Antonio Negri). The second places this reading in a line of social-critical paradigms running from Guy Debord's spectacle through Jean Baudrillard's simulation to Mark Poster's mode of information, and then to Hardt and Negri's and Carlo Vercellone's cognitive capitalism. The third part is Sun's critical evaluation, organised under three headings.

In Sun's account, Virno treats immaterial labour as the leading measure of general intellect and says it now creates value directly. Negri holds that "fixed capital is man himself", so that the line between dead and living labour dissolves. Cognitive capitalists periodise capitalism into mercantile, industrial and cognitive stages. Sun replies that Marx meant a society's total "general social knowledge", not individual faculties. Sun also says the autonomists confuse general intellect with the historically changing forms through which it becomes a direct productive force, and ignore that immaterial labour still depends on means of labour. Sun adds that value still rests on abstract labour, so capital absorbs general intellect even in its new form.

Sun concludes that the autonomists overstate how far mass intellect has spread. Any such intellect remains capital-dominated, and Marx's full unity of individual, mass and universal intellect belongs to communism. Sun also argues that Marx distinguished immaterial labour that produces surplus value from labour that does not. On Sun's reading, the rise of such labour changes the composition of the working class, as in Engels's "mental-labour proletariat", but leaves Marx's class logic intact. Sun finds the "multitude" a supra-class category and sees the cognitive-class theory as more consistent with Marx, though still tending towards anarchism and reformism. Read the original if you want a Marxist critique of Virno, Negri and Vercellone, built on a close reading of the Grundrisse "fragment on machines".
quoteEn: When Virno, working from the subjective dimension, defines the potentials individuals possess, such as cognition, thought, communication and linguistic dialogue, as the core of general intellect, he has plainly left Marx's context and confused the generic nature of the subject with general intellect in Marx's sense.
quoteZh: 当维尔诺基于主体维度，把个体蕴含的各种潜能，如认知、思考、交往、语言对话等，界定为一般智力的核心内涵时，显然已经脱离了马克思的语境，混淆了主体自身的类属性和马克思意义上的一般智力。

t: The exception without exception in the logic of capital, and non-labour as labour
st: A critical reflection on contemporary Western left-wing thought
zh: 资本逻辑中无例外的“例外”与非劳动的劳动
zhSub: 对当代西方左翼思潮的一种批判性反思
source: Theoretical Trends Abroad (Guowai lilun dongtai), 2020 no. 4
paras: Writing against the background of the 2020 Covid-19 pandemic, Xia Ying and Huang Jing'ou ask why contemporary Western left-wing thinkers, for all their radical posture, offer so little purchase on capitalism.
