The new statutes restore Marxism-Leninism and scientific socialism as the guiding ideology and bring back democratic centralism, a move defended by General Secretary Enrique Santiago. The party also hardened its stance on the European Union, calling for exit from the eurozone and a break with the EU. Finally, it sought broader popular unity, turning United Left into a social movement and widening electoral alliances such as the one with Podemos. On causes, Yu stresses that moderation failed to stop the shrinking of the party's social base, with membership falling to about 8,800, and that internal democracy produced factionalism and weakened ties to trade unions and social movements. Externally, the crisis fuelled Euroscepticism in Spain, and the rise of Podemos displaced the party as the main radical left force.

Yu concludes that the turn is not a simple return to the old line but an attempt to build a new identity combining tradition with new issues such as feminism and environmentalism. Two questions remain open: whether the new line can be turned into action, given continuing dissent from defenders of Eurocommunism and a still factional party, and whether it can bring revival. Yu sees the PCE as one of several European communist parties adjusting their theory, and expects a hard road for all of them. Read the original if you study European communist parties, Eurocommunism or the Spanish radical left and want a Chinese academic account of the PCE's 2016–2017 turn.
quoteEn: For a PCE trying to escape crisis through change, two questions deserve attention.
quoteZh: 对试图通过变革摆脱危机的西共而言, 有两个问题值得关注。

glossary.explanation: A current among Western European communist parties from the 1960s–70s that rejected the Soviet model and favoured parliamentary, multi-party roads to socialism. The PCE under Santiago Carrillo was one of its leading exponents.
A Leninist organisational principle combining discussion with unity in action under a single central leadership. The PCE abolished it in 1991 and reintroduced it in its 2017 statutes.
The Spanish left coalition (Izquierda Unida) founded in 1986 around the PCE and smaller radical left groups. It was registered as a party in 1992.
A left-populist Spanish party that grew out of the 2011 protest movement and rose sharply from 2014. The article presents it as a main rival to the PCE.

t: Foreign left-wing scholars' critique of the capitalist world-system
zh: 国外左冀学者关于资本主义世界体系的批判
paras: Writing in 2019, Zhou Miao examines how left-wing scholars outside China, especially world-systems theorists, have criticised the capitalist world-system. The article starts from the claim that this system has become an instrument for plundering the resources and wealth of developing countries. Zhou argues that these critiques can help rebut Western accusations that China practises "neo-colonialism" through its investment and aid. They can also help explain a community with a shared future for mankind to international audiences.

The article has two main parts. The first returns to Marx and Engels on world history, the world-system and the human community, and then to the proposal of a community with a shared future for mankind. The second part surveys the foreign left under three headings: predatory accumulation, an unequal international division of labour, and a structural system of hegemony. Thinkers cited include Giovanni Arrighi, François Chesnais, David Harvey, Samir Amin, Immanuel Wallerstein, William I. Robinson, Clemente Ruiz Durán and Theotonio dos Santos.

Zhou reads the foreign scholars as continuing Marx and Engels's idea that capitalism created world history and subordinated backward countries to advanced ones. On accumulation, Zhou presents Arrighi and Chesnais on financialisation, and Harvey's "accumulation by dispossession", in which debt traps and crisis management transfer wealth from poor to rich countries. Amin's contrast between autocentric and dependent accumulation explains why underdevelopment persists. On the division of labour, Wallerstein's core, semi-periphery and periphery, and the value-chain analyses of Robinson and Ruiz Durán, show high-value stages kept in the core. Dos Santos's "industrial-technological dependence" is added. On hegemony, Amin and Wallerstein describe how the United States and the institutions it dominates impose their rules on others.

Zhou concludes that predatory financialised accumulation led by private monopoly capital, together with dependent accumulation in backward countries, produces irreconcilable contradictions. In Zhou's account, these are the root cause of financial crises, sluggish growth and the new difficulties facing globalisation. Xi Jinping's call for a community with a shared future for mankind is presented as a continuation of Marx and Engels's thought on community and as a Chinese contribution to reforming global governance. Read the original if you want a Chinese Marxist overview of how world-systems and dependency theorists are being used to frame China's international discourse.
quoteEn: The capitalist world-system is an unequal, structural system.
quoteZh: 资本主义世界体系是一个不平等的结构性体系

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since around 2013 as the guiding idea of China's foreign policy. It stresses interdependence, cooperation and shared development among states.
A school associated with Immanuel Wallerstein, Giovanni Arrighi and others. It analyses capitalism as a global system divided into core, semi-peripheral and peripheral zones.

David Harvey's term, rendered in the article as predatory accumulation, for the continuing use of primitive-accumulation methods such as privatisation, financial manipulation and debt crises to transfer assets to capital.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: Humanism or structuralism? On Adam Schaff's critique of Althusser's structuralist Marxism
zh: 人道主义还是结构主义？——评沙夫对阿尔都塞结构主义马克思主义的批判
paras: Yan Yan revisits the dispute between the Polish humanist Marxist Adam Schaff and the French structuralist Louis Althusser. Their books of 1965 (Schaff's Marxism and the Human Individual, Althusser's For Marx) took opposite positions on humanism but did not engage directly. In the 1970s Schaff mounted a full critique in Structuralism and Marxism, calling Althusser's project a pseudo-Marxism and pseudo-structuralism. Yan treats this as a debate inside Marxism and asks who is right. The answer is mixed: Schaff identifies real conceptual confusions, but his critique is over-emotional and often unfair.

The article is organised around four contested themes, followed by a short assessment. These are the opposition between ideology and science; anti-empiricism versus idealism; anti-historicism versus what Schaff calls Eleaticism; and anti-humanism. Yan reconstructs Althusser's positions, then Schaff's replies, and tests both against Marx and Engels. Sources include Althusser's For Marx and Reading Capital, Schaff's History and Truth, and Karl Mannheim's theory of ideology.

Yan reports that Schaff accuses Althusser of treating ideology as false consciousness and so, like Mannheim, sliding into relativism. Schaff defines ideology as a set of views on social goals determined by class interest, and holds that the knowledge of a rising class can be scientific. Yan finds Schaff unfair here, since Althusser had widened the concept, though Althusser's vagueness is blamed. On empiricism, Schaff argues that Althusser attacks a private version of the term, confuses empiricism with positivism and mechanical reflection theory, and drops reflection theory itself. His 'two objects' theory is judged idealist and Kantian. On humanism, Schaff argues that Althusser redefines 'historicism' and 'humanism' and then rejects them. For Schaff, social relations are formed by people and should come under their control, and Marx's mature categories rest on a humanist standpoint.

Yan concludes that Schaff is most persuasive on Althusser's loose and shifting use of terms, which created theoretical confusion. Yan also faults Schaff for passing over Althusser's strengths. These include the critique of Hegel's continuous historical time, the insistence that capitalist relations are invisible, and the inquiry into Marx's problematic, though Yan reserves judgment on the 'epistemological break'. Yan holds that humanism and structuralism are not mutually exclusive in Marx, and quotes Schaff that structural analysis follows from Marxist method. The dispute will continue within Marxism. Read the original if you study Althusser, Schaff or the humanism–structuralism debate and want a Chinese scholar's balanced assessment.
quoteEn: Humanism, historicism and empiricism were all given completely different meanings by him, which indeed caused a certain theoretical confusion.
quoteZh: 人道主义、历史主义、经验主义都被他赋予了完全不同的涵义，这确实在理论上造成了一定的混乱。

t: Re-examining the "crisis of measure" in cognitive capitalism
zh: 重审认知资本主义语境中的“度量危机”问题
source: Journal of Huazhong University of Science and Technology, 2018 no. 4
paras: Writing in 2018, Sun Liang takes up a claim shared by Michael Hardt, Antonio Negri and theorists of cognitive capitalism: that immaterial and biopolitical labour cannot be measured by labour time, so Marx's labour theory of value has lapsed and a way opens toward a world of common wealth. Sun calls this the "crisis of measure". The article argues that it is a false problem, resting on a misreading of what Marx's value theory is about.

The article first sets out the cognitive-capitalist position. It distinguishes mercantile, industrial and cognitive capitalism, treats post-operaismo (post-workerism) and cognitive capitalism as near-identical, and outlines two forms of immaterial labour: intellectual or linguistic labour and affective labour. It draws on Hardt, Negri, Carlo Vercellone, Christian Fuchs and Heesang Jeon. It then turns to Marx's value-form analysis and the passages on formal and real subsumption of labour under capital, and ends with the political stakes of the "common".

Sun's central move is that the theorists treat value as a substance, a measurable quantity of labour time, and so leave Marx's analysis of value form untouched. Following Heesang Jeon, Frederick Harry Pitts and Slavoj Žižek, Sun holds that abstract labour is a historical, social category, not an expenditure of physical energy. For Marx, the question is why labour takes the form of value at all, and quantity appears only as price. Even critics and defenders who argue over quantification therefore share the same mistake, and the cognitive-capitalist view stays within classical political economy.

Second, Sun argues that digital and immaterial labour is use-value production brought under capital through real subsumption and the capitalist application of general intellect. It is not "abstract labour" in Marx's sense. Citing Marx on machinery and on capital as a "living contradiction", Sun holds that general intellect could free time only if the capitalist mode of production were transformed. Cognitive capitalism, in this reading, ignores private ownership of the means of production and overstates the subject pole of labour against capital. Read the original if you want a Marxist rebuttal of Hardt and Negri's claim that immaterial labour defeats value theory, built on value-form analysis and the subsumption texts.
quoteEn: Therefore, the "crisis of measure" is an utterly false problem.
quoteZh: 因而，“度量危机”便是一个十足的假问题

glossary.explanation: A term for a supposed new phase of capitalism in which knowledge, information and immaterial labour drive accumulation. It is used by Negri, Vercellone and others in the post-operaismo tradition.
A concept from Maurizio Lazzarato, developed by Hardt and Negri, for labour producing ideas, symbols, services and affects instead of material goods.
Sun's name for the claim that labour time can no longer measure value under cognitive capitalism, which would undermine the labour theory of value.
The theory, taken from Ricardo and developed by Marx, that the value of commodities derives from socially necessary labour.
Marx's distinction between capital taking over an existing labour process (formal) and remaking the labour process on a capitalist basis (real).
A notion from Marx's Grundrisse for socially accumulated knowledge that becomes a direct productive force. Post-workerist authors use it to argue for a communist potential.

t: The political predicament of modernity critique in contemporary Western left-wing thought, and a way out
zh: 当代西方左翼思潮现代性批判的政治困境及其出路
source: Journal of Southwest University (Social Sciences Edition), 2019 no. 1
paras: Contemporary Western left-wing thought has produced radical discourses on nearly every field, from post-Fordism and postcolonial studies to ecological Marxism and biopolitics. Zhuo and Hu argue that this proliferation conceals a political retreat. In their account, no unified left programme aimed at changing the world survives, and "left" has itself become a sign of disagreement. They call this the political predicament of the Western left's critique of modernity.

The authors attribute the predicament to two causes. One is a shift in aim from an alternative to capitalism to a critique of modernity. The other is an anti-essentialist stance that leaves no consensus on basic values or theoretical premises. The article first traces the loss of consensus from 1968 through Habermas, Lyotard, Laclau and Mouffe, Žižek and Rancière. It then examines four political issues: technology, globalisation and community, the local and indigeneity, and the politics of production. These are discussed through Paul Virilio, Zygmunt Bauman, Appadurai, Dirlik, Mamdani and Burawoy.

Zhuo and Hu contend that anti-essentialism, drawn from structuralism, makes any fixed goal such as socialism impossible, so left politics becomes endless critique with no construction. They read Laclau, Mouffe and Žižek this way, and they treat pluralist positions as close to a "third way". The four issues show, they say, that the left does not lack insight, but that these discourses either are absorbed by power or never become political. Bauman is singled out as the most conscious of the need for political commitment, since he criticises cultural pluralism as submission to reality and sets out to rebuild the public sphere and community. Dirlik, Mamdani and Burawoy are read as treating the local, the indigenous and the labour process as sites of independent political creation, not as returns to an essentialised place.

The authors conclude that without the historical condition of the capitalist mode of production and a commitment to an emancipatory agenda, critique becomes empty intellectual satisfaction. They call for a return to Marxism and for rethinking alternatives to capitalism through today's major political issues. They endorse Terry Eagleton's defence of Marx and describe Marx as the horizon of modern critique that has not yet been surpassed. Read the original if you want a Chinese Marxist assessment of Western left theory that links Bauman, Virilio, Dirlik and Burawoy to the question of political commitment.
quoteEn: If the historical condition of the capitalist mode of production is avoided, and if there is no commitment to an emancipatory agenda, critique itself becomes meaningless intellectual satisfaction and the radical stance a purely empty gesture.
quoteZh: 如果回避资本主义生产方式这个历史条件, 如果缺乏解放议程的承诺, 批判本身将成为无意义的知识满足, 激进立场则流为纯粹空洞的姿态。

t: Marxism and a new strategy for the North American left
st: An account of the 2018 Left Forum in New York
zh: 马克思主义与北美左翼新战略
zhSub: 2018年纽约左翼论坛述论
source: Studies on Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping Theories, 2018 no. 8
paras: This is a report and commentary on the 2018 Left Forum, held on 1–3 June 2018 at John Jay College of Criminal Justice, City University of New York. Zhang and Zhang describe it as the most important gathering of the North American left. Its theme was "Crafting a New Strategy for the Left", and the organisers called for a broad left coalition that overcomes divisions such as class versus identity and reform versus revolution.

The authors first outline the event: opening, plenary and closing sessions with speakers including Richard D. Wolff, Gayle McLaughlin, Gerald Horne and Ajamu Baraka. There were also 266 panels in eight thematic tracks, plus plays and film screenings. They then summarise panel positions under four headings: Marxism as method and system of thought; Trump and the international order; the need for an independent left party; and their own closing comments.

On Marxism, the authors report panelists (among them Kevin Anderson, David Harvey, David Kotz and Peter Hudis) arguing that Marx's class theory, analysis of finance, dialectics and theory of alienation remain essential for analysing twenty-first-century capitalism. Some urged organising North American movements in the light of twentieth-century socialist revolutions. Panels on Trump, in the authors' account, blamed capitalism for inequality, debt and democratic corruption, and described "Trumpism" as destabilising through militarism and attacks on reproductive rights. Other panels argued that the proletariat remains the revolutionary class and that an independent working-class or left party is needed, though some speakers conceded that conditions for it do not yet exist.

In their own assessment, the authors judge that some of the views have value and that the forum shows Marx's lasting influence. They also identify limits. In their view, some participants rely on the "hope of change" rather than thorough revolution. The forum, they note, has called for an independent party for several years without a unified leadership or the personnel and funds to build one. They also consider the aim of competing in bourgeois electoral politics unattainable. Read the original if you want a Chinese academic's panel-by-panel survey of the 2018 Left Forum and a view from China on the strategic limits of the US left.
quoteEn: But without a unified leadership body and corresponding human, material and financial support, this goal will be difficult to achieve.
quoteZh: 但是, 如果没有统一的领导机构和相应的人力物力财力做支撑, 这一目标将难以实现。

t: Discourse-based justice and recognition-based justice
st: A comparative analysis of the conceptions of justice of Habermas and Honneth
zh: 基于商谈的正义与基于承认的正义
zhSub: 哈贝马斯与霍耐特两种正义观的比较分析
paras: Kong and Huang compare two conceptions of justice from the Frankfurt School: Jürgen Habermas's justice grounded in discourse (商谈, often rendered "discourse" or "deliberation") and Axel Honneth's justice grounded in recognition. They argue that Honneth, Habermas's student, supplies the ethical dimension that Habermas's legal-procedural theory underdevelops. They also argue that both theories remain abstract and formal, and detached from material interests.

The article has three parts. The first reconstructs Habermas's theory of the legitimacy of rights in Between Facts and Norms, drawing on his earlier Reconstructing Historical Materialism. The second turns to Honneth's "struggle for recognition" and his three principles of recognition-based justice. The third part is a short conclusion, which brings in Nancy Fraser's Marxist-inflected critique of both thinkers.

On Habermas, the authors argue that legitimacy, distinct from mere legality, is the precondition of justice, and that rights can only originate in intersubjective discourse conducted under idealised, coercion-free conditions. They stress the public sphere, which they distinguish from Rawls's veil of ignorance as a communicative structure rooted in a civil society of non-governmental, non-economic associations. They add that mutual recognition is already implicit in Habermas's idea of valid, discourse-based consensus. Honneth reverses the order. In his view the equality and rationality Habermas presupposes cannot be taken for granted, so recognition must be fought for. Drawing on Hegel and Mead, he derives principles of need (love and self-confidence), equality (legal recognition and self-respect) and contribution (social esteem and solidarity). The authors see his view as an alternative between liberalism and communitarianism. They fault it for treating distribution as a moral matter of recognition, cut off from the mode of production, so that it ignores the structural causes of unjust distribution. They add that achievement-based distribution could even widen social divisions.

In the conclusion, the authors speak of a "family resemblance" between the two thinkers: both rest on abstract, formal intersubjective relations. They note that Habermas replaced Marx's historical materialism and class struggle with communicative theory in 1976, and that Honneth's recognition likewise has no bearing on substantive redistribution. They present Fraser's revival of redistribution and Marx in the early 2000s debate as evidence that historical materialism retains theoretical and practical significance. Read the original if you study Habermas, Honneth and the Frankfurt School, or want a Chinese Marxist assessment of recognition theory and the redistribution debate.
quoteEn: However "rational" and "fair" intersubjective discourse may be, and however respectfully subjects "recognise" one another, both remain aloof, far from the entanglements of real social "interests" and from discrimination between classes (or races) and substantive inequality.
quoteZh: 无论主体间的商谈如何“合理”和“公平”, 或者, 无论主体间是如何相互尊重地“承认”, 它们都仍然是高高在上, 远离了现实社会的“利益”纠葛, 远离了阶级 (种族) 之间的歧视或实质上的不平等。

t: From natural things to speculative realism
st: The evolution of contemporary European theories of the object
zh: 从自然物到思辨实在论
zhSub: 当代欧洲对象理论的演进
paras: Writing in 2018, Lan Jiang asks why European philosophy is now reviving the question of the object, and how the object should be understood in an age of the internet and digitalisation. The article names Alain Badiou, Bruno Latour, Quentin Meillassoux, Tristan Garcia, Graham Harman, Ray Brassier and others as part of this revival. Lan's thesis is that the new theories can only be understood by returning to the longer history of thinking about things, which leads to a 'speculative turn' that tries to think objects beyond human knowledge and signs.

The article moves through five sections. It begins with the object as natural thing in pre-Socratic thought, then Plato, Descartes' subject–object scheme and Kant's thing-in-itself. It then sets out two modern routes: vitalism (Marx's practical conception of the object, Whitehead, Bergson, Deleuze and Guattari, and the e-flux art platform) and semiotics (Peirce, Roland Barthes, Jean Baudrillard). The fourth section turns to Gilbert Simondon, Yuk Hui, object-oriented programming and speculative realism, and a short conclusion follows.

Lan argues that the object has never been a neutral given. For Descartes it is a relation structured by the subject's reason, and Kant's thing-in-itself marks what that structure cannot reach. Vitalism treats things as flux that cognition cuts into separate individuals, while semiotics treats the object as a sign whose value lies in social distinction, so that Lan reads Marx's and Lukács's reification as a matter of sign exchange. Lan credits semiotics with explaining objects produced to fill gaps in a sign system, as in digital games, but notes that it reduces things to a system of valuation, so the object escapes it.

Simondon's 'technical object' and Hui's 'digital object' are presented as a turning point: such objects are convergent ensembles whose recognition depends partly on non-human, machine procedures. Meillassoux's attack on correlationism and Harman's object-oriented ontology, drawing on object-oriented programming, are read as attempts to break the tie between human subject and object. Lan concludes that the speculative turn is only a first step and has not given precise answers. Old epistemic equipment is insufficient for strange new objects, and thinking must follow technological development. Read the original if you want a historical map of European object theory, from Greek philosophy to speculative realism, linked to digital technology.
quoteEn: The speculative turn in thinking about the object today has only taken the first step.
quoteZh: 今天的关于对象思考的思辨转向, 仅仅只是迈出了第一步

t: Western Marxism in the perspective of the history of Marxism's development
zh: 马克思主义发展史视野中的西方马克思主义
source: Journal of Party and Government Cadres (Dangzheng ganbu xuekan), 2018 no. 4
paras: Ma Yongjun asks how Western Marxism should be placed within the whole history of Marxism, and what Chinese scholars can still learn from it. Citing Xi Jinping's 2016 remarks that Western researchers did solid work on Marxist texts, and his 2017 call to study foreign Marxism neither rejecting it wholesale nor copying it wholesale, Ma rejects two sectarian stances: dismissing Western Marxism outright, and treating it as the only orthodoxy. The article argues that it should be studied, with its flaws acknowledged, to help reunite theory and practice.

The article has three parts: the origins of Western Marxism, why it reached a dead end, and the practical significance of placing it in the history of Marxism. Ma starts from the split after Marx's death among Kautsky's dogmatism, Bernstein's revisionism, and the left of the Second International (Lenin and Rosa Luxemburg). The later sections turn to the Frankfurt School, Lukács, Gramsci, Althusser and the events of May 1968, then to the reception of Western Marxism in China since reform and opening up.

Ma traces Western Marxism to Luxemburg and treats it as the theoretical heir of her Marxism of advanced countries, as Leninism and its Chinese successors were its practical counterpart in backward ones. Ma credits it with depth, the dialectical method, totality, subjectivity and practice. Ma attributes its failure to three congenital defects. It set Lenin against Luxemburg and Marx against Engels, which Ma calls sectarian. It split Marxism's scientific and revolutionary sides, for example humanism against scientism and critical theory against developmental theory. And it withdrew from parties and the masses into intellectual circles. In Ma's account, it moved from philosophy back away from political-economy critique, and its theoretical radicalism turned into practical conservatism, ending in bankruptcy in 1968.

Ma credits the introduction of Western Marxism with lifting Chinese Marxist philosophy beyond the old textbook system, and says it still offers resources on democracy, human development, ecology and consumerism, even though some Chinese scholars repeated its errors. Ma argues that the post-2008 problem of overcapacity, and the "new normal" of economic development, bring Luxemburg's Accumulation of Capital and Marx's six-volume plan back into view. The article calls for drawing lessons from the Second International, Stalin's model and Western Marxism, and for returning both to Marx and to real life. Read the original if you want a Chinese scholar's defence of studying Western Marxism, framed by a Luxemburg-to-Lenin genealogy and the Party leadership's official guidance on foreign Marxism.
quoteEn: However mistaken the conclusions of Western Marxism may be, the serious way in which Western Marxists studied the classic works is at least worth learning from.
quoteZh: 无论西方马克思主义的结论如何错误, 至少西方马克思主义者认真研究经典著作的做法是值得我们学习的。

glossary.explanation: The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in China in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.

t: An analysis of the impact of left-wing governments in Latin America on democratic political development since the end of the twentieth century
zh: 试析20世纪末以来拉美左翼执政对民主政治发展的影响
source: Latin American Studies (Lading Meizhou Yanjiu), 2018 no. 5
paras: Fang asks how the left-wing governments that came to power in Latin America from the end of the twentieth century affected democratic political development, a wave the author says began to recede in 2015. The thesis is that the effects were mixed and cannot be described simply as progress or regression. Fang holds that the outcome depended on whether a government was radical or moderate.

The article first traces the left's shift from rejecting 'bourgeois' democracy and armed struggle in the 1960s and 70s to embracing electoral democracy after the 'third wave' of democratization. It then compares the left's critique of Latin America's 'democratic deficit' and its calls to 'deepen democracy'. Next it surveys practice in two groups of cases: radical governments (Chávez's Venezuela, Morales's Bolivia, Correa's Ecuador) and moderate ones (Lula and Rousseff in Brazil, Uruguay's Broad Front, Chile). It ends by assessing consequences.

Fang argues that radical governments made participatory democracy their goal, through new constitutions, referendums, communal councils in Venezuela, 'consensus democracy' in Bolivia and new citizen-participation bodies in Ecuador. The author credits them with greater inclusion of Indigenous people, the poor and other excluded groups, and with higher satisfaction with democracy for a time. Fang also finds they concentrated power in the presidency, weakened checks and balances, curbed pluralism and deepened polarization, above all in Venezuela. Moderate governments, in the author's account, respected constitutional order, kept the legislature and judiciary independent and handled opponents through negotiation, but they did less to widen participation. Fang adds that all of these governments largely kept competitive elections and left office through constitutional procedures.

Fang concludes that the radical left's participatory model did not establish an alternative democratic model and in places damaged representative democracy. The author cites some scholars who regard the moderate path as more durable. With the right reviving, the article argues that every camp must tackle poverty, inequality and corruption, strengthen citizenship, checks and balances and the judiciary, and build a democratic model suited to national conditions. Read the original if you want a comparative account of Latin American left governments' democratic records, with data from Latinobarometer and constitutional detail, written from a Chinese academic perspective.
quoteEn: On the whole, Latin American left-wing politicians largely abided by the competitive principles of electoral democracy, and Latin American democratic politics withstood the test of alternation between left and right.
quoteZh: 总的来说, 拉美左翼政治家基本遵守选举民主的竞争原则, 拉美民主政治经受了左右更迭的考验。

glossary.explanation: A model in which citizens take part directly in government decisions, to supplement or partly replace representative institutions. The article treats it as the central goal of the radical left.
The dominant Western model, in which citizens elect representatives to rule on their behalf. The article describes it as limited and indirect.
The gap between the promise of democracy and its performance in meeting citizens' demands. The article uses it for Latin America's 'limited democracy' after the end of military rule.

t: On the question of labour's subjectivity in Capital
st: Based on the theory of the Japanese Uno School
zh: 论《资本论》的劳动主体性问题
zhSub: 基于日本宇野学派的理论
paras: Does labour have the status of a subject in Marx's theory? You Xinwei takes up this question, on which Chinese scholars disagree. Some, from the practical-materialist tradition, build Marx's theory on a principle of labour's subjectivity, while others hold that in Capital labour is only an instrument of capital's valorisation. Drawing on the Japanese Uno School, which is little introduced in China, the author argues that in the theoretical system of Capital labour has no subjectivity and exists only as something passive within capital's logic.

The article first contrasts the Uno School with Japan's civil-society school (Mochizuki Seiji, and Han Lixin in China), which reads Marx through labour's externalisation and early alienated labour. It then sets out four themes. The first is where the labour process sits in Capital and in Uno Kozo's 'principles' theory. The second is the Uno School reading of alienation as arising from the forms of circulation. The third is the relation between labour and the categories of Capital, and the resulting rethinking of the labour theory of value. The fourth is how capitalism can be sublated.

Following Uno, You argues that Marx deliberately treats the labour process only after commodities, money and the commodification of labour-power, as a moment of industrial capital (M–C…P…C′–M′). Uno distinguishes 'economic principles', such as the metabolism between humans and nature found in all societies, from 'economic laws', and holds that the former can be theorised only through the latter. Shimizu Masanori calls labour a 'nothing'. For him, alienation does not come from the labour process but from the commodification of labour-power, derived from the general value form in circulation. Thought therefore moves from value to labour, not the reverse, and the labour theory of value becomes a theory of the value of labour-power. For Uno, the basic contradiction of capitalism is the commodification of labour-power, so overcoming capitalism means abolishing it, not extending socialisation or nationalisation. Uno and Ouchi Hideaki see Marx's 'negation of the negation' in chapter 24 as a philosophical transition logic. Aoki Kohei looks to an external 'other', reached through stage theory and analysis of present conditions.

You concedes that the Uno School departs far from Marx, who sought to raise the standing of workers through their own efforts. The author nonetheless finds the position worth pondering. In Western societies workers are, in You's account, absorbed into capital's logic in values as well as in production, and Streeck's 'neo-Protestantism' and Marcuse's thesis are cited. You concludes that the Uno School's appeal to an 'other' to sublate capitalism offers real reference value today. Read the original if you want an introduction in Chinese to the Uno School's reading of Capital, and its contrast with practical-materialist and civil-society readings of labour.
quoteEn: It is not labour's subjectivity that determines the logic of capital; rather, the nature of labour's subjectivity must be determined by the logic of capital.
quoteZh: 不是劳动的主体性决定资本逻辑, 而是劳动主体性的性质必须被资本逻辑决定。

glossary.explanation: A Japanese school of Marxian economics founded by Uno Kozo (1897–1977). It purifies Capital into a theory of 'principles' and separates it from stage theory and analysis of present conditions.
A Japanese Marxist current, represented here by Mochizuki Seiji, that reads Marx's theory of history as the formation of civil society through human labour on nature.
The Uno School's term for the purified, abstract theory of a pure capitalist economy, which it distinguishes from stage theory and analysis of present conditions.
The process by which the capacity to work becomes a commodity sold for a wage. The Uno School treats it as the root contradiction of capitalism.

t: Rethinking the dialectics of nature
st: Based on Lukács's idea of historical dialectics
zh: 对自然辩证法的再思考
zhSub: 基于卢卡奇的历史辩证法思想
paras: Fu Zeyu asks why Georg Lukács rejected Engels's dialectics of nature, and whether that rejection holds. The article argues that Lukács's critique rests on a misunderstanding of Engels, and that Marxism's view of nature and its view of history together form a complete theoretical system. It sets out to defend Engels's dialectics of nature on that basis.

The article begins with Lukács's early project in History and Class Consciousness. This was a defence of Marxism against the Second International's \"vulgar\" Marxists, who discarded Hegel and treated Marxism as a positive science. Fu then explains Lukács's concept of historical dialectics, his account of reification and subjectivity, and his claim that only the proletariat can restore philosophical totality. The last part examines why Lukács dismissed Engels and then answers him through Marx's and Engels's own texts.

In Fu's account, Lukács treats orthodox Marxism as a method, namely dialectics of totality. It grasps facts as moments of a structured whole and unveils the reified, fetishised relations of capitalism. On this view the subject-object interaction and the unity of theory and practice are absent from our knowledge of nature, and Engels's dialectics of nature looked like the naturalism of Kautsky. Fu replies that Marx never named a \"dialectics of nature\" but pervasively treated the unity of humans and nature, humanized nature and natural laws. Fu cites Marx's letters of 1867 and 1868 and says Marx supported Engels's research. Engels, in this reading, drew dialectics out of the natural sciences rather than forcing it onto nature, and he was also answering Dühring. Fu adds that Lukács could not have read the Dialectics of Nature, which was unpublished when he wrote.

Fu concludes that reducing Marx's dialectics to historical dialectics is narrow, and that Engels filled a field Marx left undeveloped. The \"Marx–Engels opposition\" thesis, which Fu associates with Western Marxists, is therefore rejected. Fu also notes that Lukács's stress on subjectivity risks sliding into idealism and voluntarism. Read the original if you want a Chinese defence of Engels against Lukácsian and Western Marxist critiques, built on close reading of Lukács and the Marx–Engels correspondence.")
quoteEn: Therefore, to reduce Marx's dialectics merely to historical dialectics is narrow and incomplete, and highly irresponsible.
quoteZh: 所以将马克思的辩证法仅仅归结为历史辩证法是狭隘的、不全面的, 也是极不负责任的。

t: Lukács's dialectic of totality and its influence on Western Marxism
zh: 卢卡奇的总体性辩证法及其对西方马克思主义的影响
source: Studies on Marxist Theory in Higher Education (Gaoxiao Makesizhuyi Lilun Yanjiu), 2018 no. 4
paras: Why is Lukács regarded as the founding father of Western Marxism? Dong argues that the reason lies in History and Class Consciousness (1923), where Lukács defined orthodox Marxism as a method, the dialectic of totality, rather than as a body of doctrine built on economic determinism. The article contends that this move countered the Second International's vulgar materialism and revived Marxism's revolutionary character, but that it was also one-sided.

The article has four parts. It first traces the origin of the dialectic of totality in Lukács's reflection on the failure of the European workers' movement after the First World War. It then sets out the concept's content and assesses it. Finally it surveys how thinkers from Korsch and Gramsci to Fredric Jameson took up, rejected or reworked the idea, and closes with the lessons Dong draws.

Dong summarises Lukács's concept as four unities: whole and part, history and nature, subject and object, theory and practice. Lukács used these to criticise reification under capitalism and to assign the proletariat's class consciousness, mediated by the Communist Party as organisation, the role of transforming society. Dong judges that Lukács set method against content, opposed Marx to Engels by denying a dialectics of nature, inflated class consciousness and thereby retreated into Hegelianism, and so drifted from Marxism, while still enriching its dialectical thought. In the second half, Dong sorts Western Marxist responses into three paths: defending and developing totality (Korsch, Gramsci, Marcuse, Habermas, Jameson), opposing it (Adorno, Bertell Ollman), and reconstructing it (Sartre, Althusser).

Dong concludes that, despite its one-sidedness, the dialectic of totality is the methodological cornerstone of Western Marxism and a coordinate for understanding its history and likely future. The author also draws a lesson for China: a totalising perspective should guide the modernization of socialism with Chinese characteristics, coordinating economic, political, cultural, social and ecological construction and strengthening the Party's governing capacity. Read the original if you want a compact Chinese-language survey of how Lukács's totality shaped later Western Marxists, together with a critical Chinese assessment of his method.
quoteEn: Although Lukács's definition of the dialectic of totality as the essence of Marxist theory is somewhat one-sided, this methodology has become the basic means by which Western Marxist scholars observe and criticise social problems.
quoteZh: 卢卡奇将总体性辩证法思想规定为马克思主义理论本质, 虽然具有一定的片面性, 但这一方法论已然成为西方马克思主义学者是用以观察和批判社会问题的基本手段。

glossary.explanation: Lukács's account of Marxism's essence as a method that grasps society as a whole in which the whole determines the parts. Chinese scholarship treats it as the foundation of Western Marxism.

glossary.zh: 庸俗唯物主义经济决定论
glossary.explanation: The label applied to the Second International's view that economic factors alone drive history and that revolution arises spontaneously. The article follows Lukács and Korsch in criticising it.
The tradition that began with Lukács, Korsch and Gramsci and continued through the Frankfurt School and others, concerned with philosophy, culture and method.
The official name for China's current path and system. Here it frames the article's closing recommendation.

t: The internal logic of the rise and development of Western Marxology
zh: 西方马克思学兴起与发展的内在逻辑
source: Marxist Philosophy Review (Mákèsī zhǔyì zhéxué lùncóng), 2018 no. 1
paras: Li Jingxinhong and Wang Xiaonan ask why Western Marxology (Marxologie, the scholarly study of Marx's life, editions and texts) arose and kept deepening. They note that Chinese scholarship, following Soviet and East European writers, long read the term only as a Cold War ideological weapon and explained the field by external events. Cold War politics and the student-worker movements did matter, the authors concede. Their thesis is that the sustained driver was continuous internal factors: three interacting parts, three interacting stances, and a two-way relation with Western Marxism.

Published in 2018, the article has four sections. The first treats the interplay of biography, textual editing and interpretation of Marx's thought, with the successive editions MEGA1, MECW and MEGA2 as the main case. The second examines the "appreciative", "hostile" and "objective-neutral" stances, using Marx biographies from Engels, Mehring and Spargo to E. H. Carr, Isaiah Berlin, McLellan and Fetscher. The third examines how Marxology and Western Marxism relate, through Marcuse, David Harvey and the Hegel–Marx question. The fourth draws conclusions.

On the three parts, the authors argue that interpretation needed reliable biography and texts. Publishing the 1844 Manuscripts in the MEGA1 era prompted debates on humanism, the Marx–Hess relation and Althusser's "break", and later editorial work, such as the revised count of the Paris Notebooks, fed back into interpretation. On the three stances, they argue that hagiographic, hostile and neutral works provoked one another and sent all sides back to archives and manuscripts; some hostile works even supplied material that orthodox writers used. On Western Marxism, they call the two "twins" from one matrix, with the "I annotate the Classics" (Marxology) and "the Classics annotate me" (Western Marxism) modes. Marcuse moved from the first to the second, while Harvey moved the other way. Trends in Western philosophy reach Marxology through Western Marxism, as in the rise, decline and return of Hegel in Marx studies.

The authors conclude that Marxology is a self-renewing field. Its internal interactions drive a spiral of development, and exchange with Western Marxism, for instance the charge that Marx was "ecologically blind" or "gender blind", brings new questions and keeps it from becoming a closed perpetual-motion machine. They argue that this view lets Chinese scholars reassess the stereotyped Soviet-era image of Marxology and anticipate its research directions. Read the original if you want a Chinese-language account of how Western Marx scholarship developed, with detail on editions, biographies and the Hegel–Marx debate.
quoteEn: Western Marxology and Western Marxism have interacted frequently from the start; one might even say they are "twins" conceived and developed from the same matrix.
quoteZh: 西方马克思学与西方马克思主义从一开始就进行着频繁的互动, 甚至可以说, 两者是同一个母体中孕育和发展出来的“双生子”。

glossary.explanation: The term Marxologie was coined by Maximilien Rubel in 1959 for scholarly study of Marx's life, editions and texts. Soviet and East European writers often treated it as a hostile ideological project, a view the article contests.
The tradition associated with Lukács, Korsch, Gramsci, the Frankfurt School and later thinkers, which interprets Marxism through Western philosophical currents.
A Chinese scholarly idiom for faithful commentary on canonical texts. The article uses it for text-centred Marxology, in contrast to the opposite mode of 'the Classics annotate me'.
An idiom for using canonical texts to develop one's own ideas. The article applies it to the creative interpretation of Western Marxism.
The study of manuscripts and editions, here the editing and dating of Marx's works in MEGA and similar collections.

t: The ontological status of speech and its critical function
st: A study of Jacques Bidet's critical theory of modernity
zh: 言语的本体论地位及其批判功能
zhSub: 雅克·比岱的现代性批判理论研究
source: Journal of Wuhan University (Philosophy and Social Sciences Edition), 2019 no. 1
paras: Tang Zhengdong examines how the French Marxist philosopher Jacques Bidet builds a critique of modernity on the concept of speech (parole). Tang argues that Bidet pushes the critical tension in speech further than Habermas and others who read modernity through discourse. In Tang's reading, Bidet shows that the social force of categories is not a mere ideological surface but reflects the logic of class struggle. The article ultimately judges Bidet's framework subjectivist and short of historical materialism.

The article draws mainly on Bidet's Theorie generale (A General Theory), his contributions to the Dictionnaire Marx contemporain, and Exploring Marx's Capital. It moves through three themes: the ontological status of speech and the move from meta-structure to structure; the social efficacy of concepts and the critical function of speech; and the politics of common deliberation that Bidet proposes. Tang places Bidet in a line running from the French regulation school and Bourdieu to Habermas, and compares his claims with passages from Marx and Engels.

Tang's central claim is that Bidet treats the immediacy of speech as a necessary fiction with ontological standing. Speech is a proclamation that lets everything between people be re-examined, and it calls for mediations: contract, cooperation and government, with individual and central contracts containing one another. Bidet's interest lies in the antagonism between what modern society proclaims and what it actually is, and in the transition from meta-structure to structure. He reads Marx's critique of bourgeois categories as a philosophical questioning of market-only contract. He treats exploitation and ownership as contestable, reversible facts resting on a common will. Emancipation then comes through deliberative planning, public ownership and political democracy, with alliances between the people and holders of 'qualification capital'.

Tang credits Bidet with an original account of speech's critical and emancipatory role, more than with new concepts. He argues, however, that this account rests on a subjectivist reading. Bidet, in Tang's view, ignores the difference between commodity exchange in general and generalised exchange under capitalism, and does not read ownership through the internal contradictions of the mode of production. He therefore underrates the objective constraints and laws of social structure that Marx stressed. Read the original if you study Western Marxism, French Marxism or Bidet in particular, and want a Chinese philosophical assessment of his view of speech, contract and class.
quoteEn: His historicist interpretive horizon has not reached the theoretical level of historical materialism.
quoteZh: 他的这种历史主义的阐释视域并没有达到历史唯物主义的理论层面。

t: The modern predicament of Western democracy: from Marx to post-Marxism
zh: 西方民主的现代困境: 从马克思到后马克思主义
paras: Why is Western democracy losing its political force, and is capitalism or democracy itself to blame? Xie Yazhou opens with Žižek's remark on Lee Kuan Yew, Sandel's worry that Americans are losing control of the forces governing their lives, and the diagnosis of a democratic crisis by the Trilateral Commission and American neoconservatives. The article argues that Marx traced the predicament to a "civilizational defect" in the modern political sphere, not mainly to capital's logic, and that post-Marxism tries to remedy it through radical democracy.

The article has three parts. The first reconstructs Marx's early critique of the developed modern state, drawing on the Introduction to the Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right and the essay On the Jewish Question, with Rousseau and Kant as reference points. The second turns to post-Marxist thinkers, mainly Laclau and Mouffe, with Žižek, Jameson, Sandel, Habermas, Gramsci and Schmitt as interlocutors. The third offers reflections on how to leave the predicament, ending with a Chinese standpoint.

Xie's core argument is that, for Marx, the modern state rests on a conception of freedom as separation. It splits people into egoistic private individuals and an illusory political citizen, so that people cannot grasp themselves as a "species" through democratic life. The state thus abandons both people and civil society, and civil society grows by its own logic until capital absorbs and "rationalises" it, leaving politics empty. Post-Marxists such as Mouffe and Laclau share this alarm and seek to restore politics through antagonism, a plurality of political spaces, democratic citizenship and a hegemony of radical democratic values. Xie notes that this leaves the capitalist class character of democracy unchanged.

Xie concludes that only two paths exist: remedying democracy's defect so it becomes "people's democracy" able to control capitalism, or smashing the capitalist system, which the author rejects as a historical regression. Politics without a party organisational form, Xie says, is politics without politics. The article closes by contrasting Western procedural democracy with socialist democracy under the Communist Party's unified leadership, and calls for confidence in the institutions and theory of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Read the original if you want a Chinese Marxist reading of Marx's early political writings alongside Laclau and Mouffe's radical democracy, and how that reading is turned toward a defence of the Chinese political path.
quoteEn: The predicament of democracy is determined by the very nature of the modern democratic state; it is the inevitable result of the \"civilizational defect of the modern political sphere\".
quoteZh: 民主的困境正是由现代民主国家的本质所决定， 是“现代政治领域的文明缺陷”所导致的必然后果。

glossary.explanation: A current of thought, associated with Ernesto Laclau and Chantal Mouffe, that revises Marxism by stressing discourse, hegemony and plural social struggles over class-based analysis.
The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's model of socialism since reform and opening up.
The official term for China's socialist democracy, presented by the Party as serving the fundamental interests of the people, in contrast to Western liberal democracy.

t: The Sino-US trade dispute within the global trade system: an interview with Professor David Kotz
zh: 全球贸易体系下的中美贸易争端——大卫·科茨教授访谈录
paras: This is an interview conducted by Zhang Daiwei of Tsinghua University with the US Marxist economist David M. Kotz, a representative of the social structure of accumulation school at the University of Massachusetts Amherst. It took place during Kotz's visit to Tsinghua in May 2018, as the Trump administration's tariffs on steel, aluminium and Chinese goods were being announced. Kotz argues that the measures aim to contain China's rise, that the dispute so far is a trade threat rather than a full trade war, and that a trade war would damage both sides.

The interview has five parts: the background and causes of the dispute; the current global trade system and its history; the features of a more rational trade system; views on China's rise; and forecasts of how the conflict will develop. Kotz compares the dispute with the Cold War, with US–Japan relations in the 1980s and with the Smoot-Hawley tariff of 1930. He also discusses US media and public opinion, the 2018 midterm elections and the 2020 presidential race.

Kotz traces the global trade system to capitalism's drive for profit, in the spirit of the Communist Manifesto, and distinguishes regulated capitalism and the Bretton Woods order from the neoliberal system after the 1970s. He holds that this system strengthens capital against workers, and that patents on knowledge, which he calls a public good, restrict technological progress. He also says free trade freezes developing countries into their existing comparative advantage and pressures socialist economies to adopt capitalist forms. He notes that South Korea and China grew through state-led industrial policy, and that the US itself used tariffs and appropriated British textile technology, citing Ha-Joon Chang's Kicking Away the Ladder. On this basis he contends that US demands that China abandon industrial policy are contradictory.

Kotz proposes four principles for a fairer system: temporary protection for developing countries, freedom to pursue industrial policy, broad access to new technology, and permitted capital controls. He sees Made in China 2025 as an upgrading strategy rather than a bid for domination, and argues that US job losses should be met with domestic employment and welfare policies, not tariffs. He proposes dialogue in the short term, reform of the trade system in the medium term, and a world of production for need rather than profit in the long term. He says big US business opposes the tariffs but backs containing China, and that the tariff policy is Trump's personal project. Read the original if you want a US Marxist's view of the 2018 trade dispute and of Chinese industrial policy, as presented to a Chinese academic audience.
quoteEn: Development does not mean following comparative advantage, but continually changing it.
quoteZh: 发展的含义不是指跟随比较优势, 而是不断改变比较优势。

t: Globalization, anti-globalization and de-globalization from a Marxist perspective
zh: 从马克思主义视角看全球化、反全球化和逆全球化
paras: Writing in 2018, after the 2008 financial crisis and the 2016 "black swan" events (the British Brexit vote and the US presidential election), Zheng Yiming and Zhang Chaoying ask how globalization, anti-globalization and the current wave of "de-globalization" (逆全球化) should be understood from a Marxist standpoint. They argue that anti-globalization and de-globalization are both companions of globalization, which remains the main trend of world history. De-globalization, in their view, is a temporary and unsustainable "speed bump".

The article has four sections. It first grounds globalization in Marx's theory of world history; it then examines the anti-globalization movement, from the 1999 Seattle protests to critiques of neoliberalism and the "democratic deficit"; it analyses the causes of the present de-globalization wave; and it closes with a "new type of globalization" associated with China's initiatives. It draws on Marx and Engels, on Chomsky, Fukuyama, Held and McGrew, and on James Petras.

The authors reject both the view that globalization is a natural result of productive forces and the view that it is Westernization under capital. They hold that it results from both, driven by the social character of large-scale industry and the expansionary nature of capital. They separate anti-globalization, voiced by labour organisations and the marginalised against capitalist globalization, from the present de-globalization, which comes from governments and leaders in the US and UK, once the main beneficiaries. They trace its causes to the intensified basic contradiction of capitalism, deindustrialization and financialization that leave the real economy in crisis, and uneven development that widens inequality. They also cite figures on the falling ratio of world trade to world GDP in 2015.

The authors conclude that de-globalization serves monopoly bourgeois interests, lacks majority support (they note Trump's popular-vote deficit) and cannot reverse the trend. They argue that, under Xi Jinping's leadership, China's Belt and Road Initiative and the call for a community with a shared future for mankind point toward an open, inclusive, balanced and win-win globalization, which they link to Marx and Engels's idea of a "real community". Read the original if you want an example of how Chinese Marxist scholars in 2018 framed Trump-era de-globalization through world-history theory and official foreign-policy concepts.
quoteEn: Both anti-globalization and de-globalization are merely companion phenomena of globalization.
quoteZh: 无论是反全球化还是逆全球化都只是全球化的伴生物

glossary.explanation: A term for policies and sentiment that reverse economic integration, such as trade protectionism and restrictions on migration and investment. Chinese discourse became widely used it after 2016.
An initiative proposed by Xi Jinping in 2013 to build infrastructure, trade and investment links across Eurasia, Africa and beyond.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping that calls for shared security, development and values among nations.

t: Habermas in environmental thought
zh: 环境思想中的哈贝马斯
paras: Environmental scholars disagree sharply about Jürgen Habermas. Some see his social thought as useful for improving the human relationship with nature, especially through discourse-based decision-making on environmental risk. Others call his system an "ecological disaster" because of its anthropocentrism and its break with the first generation of the Frankfurt School. Gunderson and Xiao, writing in Marxism and Reality (2018), argue that both camps read Habermas accurately: he is at once an anthropocentric Kantian and a forerunner of ecological democracy.

The article first examines Habermas's critique of Horkheimer, Adorno and Marcuse and his concept of a "technical cognitive interest" in controlling nature, along with the environmental objections to it. Critics discussed include Di Nolcia, Whitebook, Vogel (as critic of the early work), Bookchin, Neilson and Eckersley. It then turns to the mature theory of communicative action and discourse ethics, sorting the environmental responses into supporters, revisionists and critics. Supporters include Brulle, Webler, Eling, Rosa, Renn and McCright, and Dietz. The revisionists are Dryzek and Eckersley, and the critics are Murphy and Kreps.

The authors' central move is to separate Habermas's early "substantive" claims about nature from his mature "procedural" theory. Critics, in their account, rightly object that the technical interest is empirically untenable and historically blind, and that Habermas abandoned the first generation's critique of the domination of nature. Supporters show that discourse-based procedures can bring the public into environmental decisions in place of technocratic expertise. Revisionists such as Dryzek and Eckersley try to extend discourse ethics to non-human interests, for example through spokespersons for nature. The authors consider the objections of Murphy (utopianism, pluralism of values) and Kreps (non-humans cannot consent) reasonable but less persuasive. They note that the ideal speech situation is presented as an attainable-but-unrealisable standard and that Dryzek's view of life-support capacity as a generalisable interest answers Murphy.

Gunderson and Xiao propose two routes for continuing the "greening" of Habermas. The first is to reconstruct his break with the first generation and combine its social ecology with communicative action theory. The second, which they regard as more practical, is to keep developing discourse-based environmental decision models while attending to the environmental critiques. They hold that Habermas's anthropocentric limits should be corrected, not that his critical theory should be discarded. Read the original if you want a systematic map of environmental readings of Habermas, from Marcuse's critics to Dryzek's and Eckersley's attempts to represent nature in deliberative democracy.
quoteEn: He is both an anthropocentric Kant and a forerunner of ecological democracy.
quoteZh: 他既是人类中心主义的康德, 又是生态民主的前辈。

t: Why has a "Marx fever" returned in the West?
zh: 西方为何再现“马克思热”
paras: Yu Haiqing asks why interest in Marx has revived in Western societies, a decade after the 2008 financial crisis and around the 200th anniversary of Marx's birth in 2018. The short commentary answers that capitalism's continuing troubles keep pushing Western observers back to Marx's analysis of capitalism.

The article surveys three groups. These are Western media and left-leaning politicians, Western intellectuals and scholars, and Western communist parties. It cites the New York Times, Quartz and Teen Vogue, Jeremy Corbyn, John McDonnell and Yanis Varoufakis, and scholars such as Immanuel Wallerstein, Slavoj Žižek, Wendy Brown and David Harvey.

Yu argues that stagnation, widening inequality, terrorism, refugee flows and populism have deepened capitalism's predicament, and even Francis Fukuyama now concedes social division and the workers' plight. In this account, media tributes, anniversary conferences, and work by Samir Amin, Richard Wolff and John Bellamy Foster refute claims that Marxism is outdated, useless or bankrupt. Communist parties in Britain, Australia, Russia, France and elsewhere held commemorations, and the US and Greek parties took part in labour and anti-austerity struggles.

Yu concludes that the repeated revivals show Marxism's vitality and its truth, because Western practice cannot avoid the general laws of capitalist development that Marx revealed. The author ties this to Xi Jinping's anniversary speech and calls for stronger confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese Marxist researchers read the 2018 Western Marx anniversary coverage.
quoteEn: The reason Marx can attract Western attention again and again is evidently that contemporary Western practice simply cannot get around the general laws of capitalist development he revealed.
quoteZh: 马克思之所以能够一再吸引西方社会关注, 显然是因为当代西方实践根本无法绕开马克思所揭示的资本主义一般发展规律。

glossary.explanation: The Communist Party of China's official name for its model of socialism, developed since reform and opening up began in 1978.

t: Socialism with Chinese characteristics from the perspective of the world-system
st: Commemorating the 40th anniversary of reform and opening up
zh: 世界体系视野下的中国特色社会主义
zhSub: 纪念改革开放四十周年
paras: Marking forty years of reform and opening up, Zhou Miao asks what world-systems theory, which the article also calls the Marxism of the world-system, can tell us about the origins, success and global significance of socialism with Chinese characteristics. The author argues that China's rise should be read against the long cycles of the capitalist world-system, and that its success lies in using that system while keeping autonomous accumulation under the basic socialist economic and political institutions.

The article has three parts. The first reviews the rise of the West and the position of backward countries, drawing on Wallerstein, Frank and the Needham question. The second turns to cycles in the capitalist world-system: Kondratieff long waves, Wallerstein's hegemonic cycles and Arrighi's systemic cycles of accumulation. The third discusses the world significance of socialism with Chinese characteristics and the international pressures on China's rejuvenation.

Zhou draws three main lines. First, world-systems scholars hold that peripheral states cannot escape their position while the capitalist world-system exists; once capital was fully internationalised in the imperialist stage, the author says, the way out lay in changing the system through another social order, namely socialism. Second, Zhou reads long-wave and hegemonic-cycle theory as showing that the American cycle is in its late phase, with financialisation and the 2008 crisis resembling earlier late-wave crises. Reform and opening up in 1978 is presented as a strategic choice that took advantage of such an opening. Third, citing Arrighi, Zhou attributes China's success to retaining the basic socialist system and autonomous accumulation while partly integrating into the world-system.

Zhou concludes that China, as the new reference point of world socialism (following Jiang Hui's periodisation of Germany, Russia and China), can strengthen the Global South and promote a new international order. Hegemonic decline, the author warns, tends to bring conflict, and the United States is described as treating China as its main challenger, so strategic vigilance and peaceful development are needed. The author calls for deepening reform while upholding the dominant position of public ownership, so that China avoids dependent accumulation. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese Marxist scholar draws on Wallerstein, Frank and Arrighi to interpret China's development path and its relations with the United States.
quoteEn: Therefore, as long as the capitalist world-system exists, backward countries cannot fundamentally change their position within it.
quoteZh: 因此, 只要资本主义世界体系存在, 落后国家就不能彻底改变在世界体系中的地位。

glossary.explanation: A school of thought associated with Immanuel Wallerstein, Andre Gunder Frank and Giovanni Arrighi that analyses capitalism as a single global system of core, semi-periphery and periphery. The article notes it is also called the Marxism of the world-system.
The policy course launched at the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping, introducing market-oriented reforms and engagement with the global economy.
The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's model of socialism since the reform era, combining public ownership as the mainstay with market mechanisms.
The question, posed by the British scholar Joseph Needham, of why modern science and industrial capitalism arose in Europe rather than in China despite China's earlier technological achievements.
A term for developing and formerly colonised countries, used in official Chinese discourse to denote China's partners among non-Western states.

t: New trends in the main international currents of thought today and how to respond
zh: 当前国际社会主要思潮新动向新趋势及应对
paras: Writing in 2018, Li Ruiqin asks which social and political currents of thought are shaping international politics since the 2008 financial crisis, and how China should respond. The article argues that these currents are diverse yet interlinked, and that they act as a major visible force on world politics. Li characterises them as plural, extreme, borderless, hard to predict and hard to control.

The article takes four currents in turn: populism in Europe and the United States, nationalism, religious extremism and terrorism, and trade protectionism with its political expression, anti-globalisation. Each section draws on the 2016–2017 events of its time: Brexit, the Trump presidency, the Austrian, Dutch and French elections, the Russian and US positions on counter-terrorism, and Western trade policy. A closing section sets out the general picture and China's response.

Li argues that neoliberal globalisation produced wealth concentration and economic anxiety, feeding left-wing populism, and identity politics, feeding right-wing populism. In Li's reading, the electoral setbacks of populists in the Netherlands, Austria and France are only a pause, because the underlying socio-economic conditions are unchanged. Nationalism is described as the seedbed from which populism, extreme nationalism and religious extremism have historically grown. Religious extremism is presented as an extremely hard problem to govern, made worse by Western interventionist counter-terrorism and by differing definitions of terrorism. Protectionism is read as the economic root of anti-globalisation, which Li sees as the West retreating once globalisation's dividends fade.

Li concludes that the currents reveal a world of heightened insecurity, low mutual trust, diffuse nostalgia and passive suspicion of the future. As a response, the author points to the Belt and Road Initiative as a way to counter protectionism and extremism and deepen globalisation, while noting that it faces great-power rivalry and hesitation among some states. Li also calls for vigilance against the infiltration of extremist ideas into China, for the protection of reform and opening up and socialism with Chinese characteristics, and for cooperation through the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, BRICS and the UN. Read the original if you want an example of how a CASS researcher in 2018 framed populism, extremism and protectionism as security and ideological challenges for China.
quoteEn: Anti-globalisation is in fact one of the forms in which the West has consistently dominated the trend of world development.
quoteZh: 逆全球化, 实际是西方一贯主导世界发展趋势的表现形态之一。

glossary.explanation: A Chinese initiative announced by Xi Jinping in 2013 to build infrastructure and economic links across Eurasia, Africa and beyond. The article presents it as a counter to protectionism.
The official name for China's current path and system, in use since the early 1980s. It combines Party leadership, a socialist market economy and reform.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in 1978. Official texts treat it as the basis of China's post-Mao development.

t: Marx is still alive, much closer than we imagine
st: Russia's spontaneous and grand commemoration of the 200th anniversary of Marx's birth
zh: 马克思还活着, 比我们想象的要近得多
zhSub: 俄罗斯自发隆重纪念马克思诞辰200周年活动
source: Cultural Soft Power (Wenhua ruan shili), 2018 no. 3
paras: Why did Russian society, 27 years after the Soviet Union abandoned Marxism-Leninism, hold so many unofficial events in 2018 to mark the 200th anniversary of Marx's birth? Li Ruiqin takes up this question and argues that the commemorations reflect a conviction, repeated across the events, that "Marx was right". In Li's account they also reflect a continuing reckoning with the Soviet collapse.

The article first surveys the events, which Li describes as non-state but national, varied and sustained. They include international forums run by the Communist Party of the Russian Federation, Moscow University and the Russian Academy of Sciences, exhibitions at the State Duma and in museums, and round tables in provincial cities such as Yakutsk, Murmansk and Novosibirsk. It then discusses their unofficial, regional and youth-driven character, and ends with four explanations for the phenomenon.

Li draws on speeches by Gennady Zyuganov, Duma deputy speaker Aleksandr Zhukov and others who cite Russian inequality, falling incomes and the oligarchs' wealth as proof of Marx's analysis. In this reading, the post-Soviet record confirms Marx's predictions about finance, concentration of wealth and global capital. Li adds that speakers repeatedly pointed to China's development under Marxist guidance as a successful practice, contrasted with Russia's experience. The article also cites Moscow University professor Alexander Buzgalin to argue that Russia still needs Marxism to understand capitalism, inequality and who holds real power.

Li concludes that after nearly three decades of upheaval, Russians can return to Marx with a calmer and more reflective attitude. Li stops short of predicting that Marxism will return to Russia, but holds that the events show Marx's ideas are still relevant there. The article is a Chinese observer's account of Russian commemorations and relies largely on speakers sympathetic to Marxism. Read the original if you want a detailed, Chinese-language inventory of the 2018 Marx bicentenary events in Russia and a view of how Chinese Marxist scholars interpret them.
quoteEn: Marx has not gone far; he is much closer than we imagine.
quoteZh: 马克思没有走远, 比我们想象的要近得多。
keywords: Communist Party of the Russian Federation

t: Foreign assessments highly affirm the achievements of China's 40 years of reform and opening up
zh: 国外高度肯定中国改革开放40年成就
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts in 2018, on the 40th anniversary of reform and opening up, Liu Xiaoyun collects favourable assessments of China's record from foreign scholars, politicians and journalists. The article's thesis is that these observers see reform and opening up as having brought not only economic take-off but all-round social progress, with significant effects on the wider world.

The piece is a compilation of quoted foreign opinion arranged in three sections. The first presents reform and opening up as the driving force behind China's entry into a new era, both domestically and globally. The second asks what explains the success and answers with the leadership of the Communist Party of China. The third treats reform and opening up as offering a Chinese approach to human problems. Quoted speakers include UN Secretary-General António Guterres, Kevin Rudd, Joseph Nye, Kerry Brown-type China specialists from Britain, Iran, India, Japan, Germany, Russia, Sri Lanka and elsewhere.

In Liu's selection, foreign commentators point to China's shift from a planned to a market economy and towards consumption- and innovation-led growth, to the poverty reduction of more than 700 million people, and to a reshaped international role through the Belt and Road Initiative. The British scholar John Ross is cited as saying, on World Bank estimates, that China contributes over 30 per cent of annual world economic growth. On the question of cause, quoted voices credit the Party's adherence to Marxism adapted to Chinese conditions, its priority on the people's interests, its timely policy adjustment, and its consultative, multi-party cooperation system. A German scholar, Wolfram Adolphi, cautions that Europeans should not understand the Party by simple analogy.

Liu concludes, through the quoted observers, that China's gradual, stability-preserving reforms offer useful experience to other developing countries, even though no country can copy them mechanically and China has not sought to export its model. The article ends by linking China's development to a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a catalogue of how foreign voices were selected and presented in Chinese official-academic discourse on the 40th anniversary of reform and opening up.
quoteEn: The great achievements of reform and opening up cannot be separated from the leadership of the Communist Party of China, which has become a broad consensus in the international community.
quoteZh: 改革开放取得的巨大成就离不开中国共产党的领导，已成为国际社会的广泛共识。

glossary.explanation: The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched under Deng Xiaoping from 1978, marking the shift from the Mao-era planned economy towards a market-oriented one.
A Chinese international infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative announced by Xi Jinping in 2013, linking China with Asia, Europe and Africa.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping, stressing shared interests and joint global governance.
The official idea that Marxism is applied and developed in line with China's concrete circumstances, producing successive theoretical systems from Mao Zedong Thought onward.
The article's wording refers to the system of multi-party cooperation and political consultation led by the Communist Party, which officials describe as a form of consultative democracy.

t: Interpreting "On Contradiction" in the perspective of the history of foreign Marxism
zh: 国外马克思主义发展史视域下的《矛盾论》解读
source: Studies on Mao Zedong Thought, 2018 no. 4
paras: Writing in 2018, Wang Zhenmin asks how Marxist thinkers outside China have read Mao Zedong's "On Contradiction", and what Chinese scholars can learn from those readings. The article argues that these interpretations are shaped by the Western philosophical currents and theoretical crises of their moment. In Wang's view they therefore often cross the line into "over-interpretation" and "theoretical transgression" (理论越界). Wang also holds that they still offer useful prompts for developing a Marxist dialectics with Chinese characteristics.

The article first sets out four general features of foreign readings. They are embedded in contemporary Western currents, they serve academic discourse more than revolution, they appear at moments of crisis for Marxism, and they use Hegel's or Marx's dialectics as an intermediary. It then traces a historical sequence of four paradigms: Louis Althusser's scientistic structuralism in the 1960s, Norman Levine's neo-Hegelian reading in the 1980s, Ian Hunt's "new dialectics" in the 1990s, and Slavoj Žižek's Lacanian Marxism in the 21st century. A final section evaluates each paradigm and lists causes of the misreadings.

Wang follows Althusser's use of the essay in three stages: first to ground his theory of overdetermination in Marx's break with Hegel, then in the symptomatic reading of Capital, and finally in his theory of ideology. Levine, in Wang's account, presents Mao as having revived a Hegelianised Leninism and so as proof that Marxism must return to Hegel. Hunt compares Mao with Marx and with Masaccia's model of contradiction, and Žižek criticises Mao for rejecting the negation of the negation. Wang judges that Althusser severs the essay from "On Practice"; that Levine over-stresses Hegel; that Hunt reduces transformation of opposites to a simple swap of positions; and that Žižek fundamentally misreads Mao's dialectic as a "negative dialectics".

Wang attributes the transgressions to five causes: Orientalist presuppositions, the habit of forcing Western concepts onto Mao's thought, the gulf between the essay's historical setting and its readers' settings, the plurality of meaning in any text, and these schools' neglect of or hostility to Engels's dialectics. Evaluation should aim less at dialogue than at drawing methodological lessons from the misreadings. Such lessons can help complete Mao's wish to rewrite "On Contradiction" and to build a Marxist dialectics with Chinese characteristics. Read the original if you want a Chinese critical assessment of how Althusser, Levine, Hunt and Žižek used "On Contradiction", with the sources they drew on.
quoteEn: The purpose of the evaluation is not merely academic dialogue, but, more importantly, to dig out what the "over-interpretations" or "misunderstandings" may leave us in the way of methods and perspectives for research.
quoteZh: 评价的目的不仅仅在于学术上的对话, 更重要的在于挖掘“过度诠释”或“误解”背后可能留给我们在研究方法、视角上的启发

glossary.explanation: A 1937 philosophical essay by Mao Zedong, usually paired with "On Practice" as the "two essays". It treats contradiction as the core of dialectics and distinguishes principal and secondary contradictions and their aspects.
The author's term for foreign readings that, in his view, go beyond the historical context and content of Mao's text and impose external frameworks on it.
